title: Record: event log and blobs
description: SPEC section 9 and D14, D15, D19. Every later feature writes events (sling sent, reply landed, agent done) and blobs (packets, UI code). The record must exist first, and its formats are API (B5).

title: core: record events and blob ids as versioned data
description:
SPEC: section 9, D14, B4, B5.

Goal: a `record` module in crates/core that owns the event and blob-id formats. No IO.

Scope:
- Event: number, time, kind, version, source, payload, and tags (machine, workspace, agent, canvas). Tags are optional except machine.
- v1 kinds with typed payloads: sling sent, reply landed, file touched (path and hash, never contents), pane moved, agent blocked, agent done.
- JSON encode and decode. A reader keeps an event with an unknown kind or unknown fields (B5).
- BlobId: a content hash (pick the hash, give the reason in a doc comment), with parse, display and a function from bytes.

Acceptance:
- Round-trip tests for every kind.
- A test decodes a stored JSON fixture that has an unknown kind and an extra field.
- The module's public interface is small: types, encode, decode, hash.

Out of scope: storage, verbs, views.

title: daemon: SQLite store for events and blobs
description:
SPEC: section 9, D14, D15, P7.

Goal: slingerd owns one SQLite file that holds the record.

Scope:
- A `store` module in crates/daemon (rusqlite with the bundled feature). Two tables: events, and blobs keyed by hash.
- Append assigns the number and the time and sets the machine tag. The log is append-only: no update, no delete.
- Read events by range and by tag and kind. Put blob is idempotent. Get blob by hash.
- A data directory with a default and a `--data-dir` flag on slingerd. Document it in docs/service.md.
- cargo-deny and machete must pass with the new dependency.

Acceptance:
- Tests use a temporary directory: append, reopen, read back in order.
- Putting the same bytes twice gives one row.
- The machine name is on every stored event.

Out of scope: verbs (next seed), copy to the always-on machine (not in v1).

title: core: canvas model, items and operations
description:
SPEC: D6, section 7 rules, B2, B4.

Goal: a `canvas` module in crates/core with the item model and operations as data.

Scope:
- Items: stroke (points, colour, constant width, time), text, box, arrow (ends can point at item ids). Each item has an id, a bounding box, an author (the user, or an agent name) and a time.
- Pages: a canvas has one or more named pages. Each item is on one page.
- Operations: add, edit, move, remove, page add, page rename, page remove. `apply(op)` is the only way to change a canvas.
- Removing an item that is already gone succeeds (B4).
- An author check: an agent may edit or remove only items it made. The user's ink cannot be changed by an agent.

Acceptance:
- Tests go through the public interface only.
- Every operation has a test, and so do the already-gone and not-the-author cases.
- The interface is small: build, apply, query. No caller sees the storage layout.

Out of scope: undo, file format, geometry queries, live items.

title: core: canvas undo and redo
description:
SPEC: D6.

Goal: undo and redo over canvas operations.

Scope:
- Each operation has an inverse. Undo applies inverses as new operations, so the history stays append-only.
- Undo is per author: the user's undo does not undo an agent's item, and the reverse.
- A moved lasso selection or one erase gesture is one undo step (group operations).

Acceptance:
- Tests: undo then redo returns the same canvas for every operation kind.
- A test with mixed user and agent operations shows the per-author rule.
- Undo with nothing to undo succeeds and changes nothing.

title: feedback: leave feedback from inside the app (command, entry, feedback.jsonl), with slinger feedback add/ls/resolve/path
description: Owner request 2026-11-11: 'There should be a leave feedback feature, like Flick has, so I don't have to leave the application for it.' Model: Flick's feedback module (its docs/feedback.md): one JSON line per note appended to feedback.jsonl, never rewritten; resolving appends a line. In slinger: a leave-feedback command in the registry (so it shows in the key overlay, the palette and the Help menu), which opens a one-line entry in the focused pane; return saves, escape cancels; a flash confirms. Each line: ts (local time with offset), text, build, and what the app was showing (workspace, canvas, page, tool; selected count when any). A verb through core -> control -> daemon -> CLI and app. CLI: slinger feedback add <text> | ls [--all] [--limit n] | resolve <ts> [note] | path, text by default and --json.

title: app: new and open workspace from inside the app (palette command and sidebar entry)
description:
The app can only switch between workspaces that are already open (a tap on a sidebar row). Neither the command palette (crates/app/src/commands/registry.rs) nor the menu has a command to make or open one, so a new workspace needs the CLI: slinger workspace open [DIR] --name <NAME>.

Wanted: make a new workspace and open a directory as one without leaving the app. The workspace_open verb exists already (the daemon and crates/control have it), so this is app work only.

Decisions needed: where it lives (a palette command, a row or button at the foot of the sidebar, or both); how the directory is picked (native open panel vs a typed path); how the name is entered for a workspace with no root; whether the window turns to the new workspace; whether close workspace belongs with it.

Related: slinger-16a66e (new, open and save-as for canvas files).

title: app: cmd+V and Flick dictation did nothing for the owner for a while, then worked again with no change (intermittent, no cause found)
description:
Owner hand check 2026-11-12 on the release bundle (target/slinger.app, built 06:13, scratch daemon /tmp/slg): 'Flick dictation does not work on the slinger side, cmd+V in general does not work'. Flick works in other apps.

Agent check the same day, same running app, cmd+V sent by System Events and by computer use:
- into a canvas text being typed: pasted (3 times).
- into the palette's search: pasted (2 times).
- debugger trace of one cmd+V: NSMenu performKeyEquivalent -> validateMenuItem reads the clipboard -> sendAction paste: -> the window reads the clipboard and dispatches Edit::Paste. The path is whole.
- not checked: the sling prompt, a page rename, plain text onto a page with no text open, a real keyboard, Flick itself.

Open questions for the owner: which place, which keyboard (a remapper?), and does Edit > Paste by pointer work there.

Seen on the way:
1. Accessibility reports Edit > Paste as disabled while the app is idle though validateMenuItem answers yes when called: the item's enabled state is stale between validations. Flick may read that state before it pastes; if so it would skip slinger. Check how Flick delivers text (cmd+V event, AX menu press, or AX value).
2. With a canvas text being typed and the palette open over it, three synthetic escapes did not close the palette. Not confirmed with a real key.
3. Not checked: whether Flick is running with its [dictation] set up, which the dictate command needs.

After a fix, redo the hand check slinger-29364d.

Owner, later on 2026-11-12: it started working again by itself, same running app. One guess (agent's): a canvas text was open for typing at 41% zoom, so pastes went into that small text and were easy to miss.
closeReason: a cause shown in code and fixed (e41e9ee): an agent UI page kept the keyboard after a click, so pastes went to it; not proven to be the cause the owner hit, see the hand-check seed

description: Owner: profiles/sessions are too restrictive; wants them to behave like normal Claude Code sessions. Today (crates/core/src/session/stream.rs args): --tools is a fixed list (Read,Glob,Grep,Bash + tools named by rules), so no Task/Agent, TodoWrite, Skill, WebFetch/WebSearch unless a rule names them, and profile.rs TOOLS (10 names) refuses rules for any other tool; --permission-mode dontAsk denies everything no rule allows (Bash is only 'slinger *' plus read-only commands); --setting-sources project,local leaves out the owner's user settings, CLAUDE.md, skills and permission rules unless agent.user_config; --strict-mcp-config loads no MCP server; a profile's rules replace Edit/Write, so a profile with no rules is read-only. Needs one decision: what stands in for the permission prompt when nobody is at a terminal (bypassPermissions, the owner's own allow rules under dontAsk, or prompts sent to the app). Supersedes the TOOLS half of slinger-d6c11e.

title: session: listen delivery: a plain Claude Code session takes slings ('slinger session listen' plus a /slinger-listen plugin command), as SPEC section 5 says
description: Owner 2026-11-12: 'what we really need is to ship a /tldraw-listen equivalent for slinger'. SPEC section 5: 'A plain Claude Code session joins the list when it starts to listen, as the send-to-agent listener does today.' Today Delivery has one kind, Process (crates/core/src/session.rs): slingerd spawns 'claude --print' under tight limits (see slinger-a1c1db). Wanted: the owner's own interactive session, with its own permissions, tools, MCP and config, is the agent. Sketch: (1) core: Delivery::Listen, a per-agent queue of pending slings, a listener's claim and its expiry; (2) control + daemon: a blocking 'session_listen' verb that registers the caller for an agent and returns the next sling (message text, packet, image crops written as files the Read tool can open); (3) cli: 'slinger session listen <AGENT>' prints one sling and exits 0, so a background Bash wakes the session; (4) plugin: /slinger-listen command that runs it in a loop, answers with canvas put, sets status; guide.md. Decisions: what a sling does when nobody listens (queue and show 'nobody listening', or fall back to the spawned process); whether a listener outranks a running process session; how the agent name is picked (workspace agent vs any name).

title: Slings that wait for a listener are lost when slingerd stops
description: The listener queue (crates/daemon/src/listeners.rs) is in memory. A sling that waits is in the record (sling_sent) but no listener gets it after a restart. Rebuild the queue from sling_sent events with no session and no reply_landed, or persist it.

title: A listener that dies while it works on a sling stays attached
description: session::listen::Listener::attached is true while working, until the listener asks again. A Claude Code session that took a sling and was closed keeps the agent's slings going to a listener that is gone (the app shows working, not nobody listens). session start/stop releases it. Give working a deadline, or let status set done end it.

title: A new workspace's agent should get every tool by default
description: Today an agent with no limit fields runs only the slinger CLI, read-only commands, Edit and Write (docs/workspace.md, 'The agent's limits'; slinger-a33c, slinger-05ad22). The owner wants the default to be all tools, with limits something you opt into. Three gaps: (1) no way to say 'all tools' in agent.tools: no wildcard, so the file must list all ten built-ins. (2) MCP cannot work at all: crates/core/src/session/stream.rs always passes --strict-mcp-config with no --mcp-config, so no MCP server loads, even with user_config = true; an mcp__ rule in agent.tools is accepted but allows a tool that is never there. (3) --tools is built from the ten names in profile::TOOLS, so other Claude Code built-ins (Agent, Skill, TodoWrite and the like) can never be given. Decide the new default (and a wildcard or 'unlimited' field, and how MCP servers load), then change crates/core/src/workspace/profile.rs, session/stream.rs, docs/workspace.md, docs/service.md 'Limits' and the guide.

title: Set up and start a workspace's agent without leaving slinger

A workspace with an agent whose process is not running gives no sign in the app and no way to start it there. Wanted: from the app, make a workspace, give it an agent and its limits, and see and start its agent; and an agent that starts on its own when its workspace opens or on the first sling. Related: slinger-29bb9f (defaults to no tools).

title: design: decide O3, what the thinking record shows, now the log has real events

It has them now (sling sent, reply landed, file touched, agent blocked, agent done). Decide what the view shows and where: the owner's note on the slinger-dev canvas (2026-11-12) describes it as 'a log/trace of thinking'. Close O3 in SPEC.md with the decision. Agent presence on the canvas is meant to be the live end of this same view, so decide the two together.

title: agent presence on the canvas: a mark where an agent is reading or about to write

Show a quiet mark on the canvas at the items an agent is reading and at the place it is about to write, while it works, and remove it when the agent is done. It must not become a chat window or a text dump. It is the live end of the thinking record (SPEC 9, O3): the same log events, shown where they happen as they happen, so it draws from the log and adds no second store. Open: which events carry a place (packet read, crop, put, edit), what the mark looks like at each zoom, and how it reads with several agents on one page.

The same happened on t1068 and t1806: in a crop the owner's ink sits on top of the agent's text, which they would not have written over. So the app's text layout (line height or font metrics) and the core's box for a text item disagree. Effects: 'put --beside' leaves gaps or lands on ink, the packet's box for a text item is wrong, and an agent cannot tell which paragraph a note of the owner's sits beside. title: daemon: a sling sent while the agent is mid-turn leaves 'pending' stuck above 0, so the app shows the agent 'working' forever
description: Seen live 2026-11-12 on agent slinger-dev: session show said status done, process running at 0.1% CPU, pending 3, and the app showed '<agent> working' with nothing happening. Cause: crates/daemon/src/processes.rs adds 1 to Heard.pending for each message written to stdin (send) and takes 1 away for each answer read from stdout (listen). When a message arrives while a turn is running, Claude Code folds it into that turn (transcript: queue-operation enqueue then remove, at 05:21:38Z, 05:29:21Z and 05:34:18Z in session 6e252971), so two messages get one answer and pending leaks by 1 each time. Nothing but a process restart clears it. The app reads pending > 0 as working (crates/app/src/scene/sidebar.rs Status::of; crates/app/src/backend/sling.rs 'over' needs pending == 0), so every later sling also never reads as over. Likely the cause of slinger-9fe67e (the box that gets stuck) and part of slinger-7d5db9. Fix: do not count answers against sends; set pending to 0 when a result arrives with no turn running, or follow the turn state from the stream itself. Add a test with a stand-in agent that answers two messages with one result.

title: canvas text fills under half its box's width in the app: the core wraps at one character per 'size', the app draws a proportional font
description: Owner's hand check on the slinger-dev canvas, page 2026-11-13. On an agent's text (t2245, size 800, box 3200 wide) the owner bracketed the width the app shows, about 1390 units, and wrote 'So narrow, why?'. Cause, read from the code: crates/core/src/render/raster.rs columns() gives a line w/size characters, a square cell per character, as the crop's bitmap font draws. Since 608cae4 the app draws those same rows, in the system font at 0.83 of the size (crates/app/src/scene/glyphs.rs FONT), where a character is about 0.45 of a size wide. So the rows and the height agree with the core, and every row ends at about 43 percent of the box. The owner then writes in the empty right part of the box, and 'put --beside' leaves that space unused. Fix in one place: the core's cell should be the width the app's font has (about half a size), with the crop's font drawn to that cell, so the box, the crop and the app agree in both directions.

title: pen-less use: keyboard and mouse as a full way in, for notes without a tablet
description: Owner, 2026-11-20: slinger should work with keyboard and mouse as well as with tablet and pen. The pen stays the primary input, but with no tablet at hand slinger is still the main place for notes, ideas and thinking. Audit the same day: pan, zoom, tools, pages, panes, sling and item cut/copy/paste work without a pen. title: launcher: the app starts slingerd itself; one install, no shell step
description:
[launcher] The .app already installs to /Applications through `scripts/bundle.sh --install`, so Spotlight and the Dock can launch it, though with a generic icon. The real gap is that the app never starts slingerd, and the repo ships no launchd unit. Until someone runs slingerd from a shell, the app is a dead window that tells the user to type `slingerd --socket /var/folders/...`. Today's daemon (ppid 1) was started by a shell and left orphaned, not run by a service manager. Restarting after an update, starting after login, and finding claude on PATH are all manual shell steps. Nothing detects version skew between the app and the daemon. Recommendation: ship slingerd and slinger inside the bundle and have the app start the daemon when none answers. The daemon locks its socket and data directory, so a second copy exits with code 4 and spawning is race-safe. Add a version handshake verb so the app can offer to restart an outdated daemon. Later, add a SMAppService login item.
- (high, M, verified) App never starts slingerd; without it the window is dead and asks for a shell command. scripts/bundle.sh:10-11 (app neither ships nor starts slingerd); README.md:41; control/src/client.rs:307-310 hint "start it with 'slingerd --socket ...'" shown in the sidebar (scene.rs:417-425) and the title (scene/title.rs:105). Running slingerd pid 92917 has ppid 1, so a shell or agent started it. Direction: Bundle slingerd and slinger in Contents/MacOS. When a connect is refused or no socket exists, the app backend spawns the bundled slingerd detached (setsid, log in the data dir) and waits for the named socket. The existing locks make this race-safe. Replace the shell hint with a 'Starting slingerd' state or a Start button.
- (high, M, verified) No launchd agent or login item; the daemon dies on reboot or when its terminal closes. docs/service.md:1235 'The repo ships no launchd or systemd unit'. ~/Library/LaunchAgents has no slinger entry. daemon/src/lib.rs:215 traps only SIGTERM and SIGINT, so SIGHUP from a closed terminal kills it. Direction: Ship Contents/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist with BundleProgram set to the bundled slingerd and KeepAlive on. Register it with SMAppService through an app setting ('Start at login'), so it shows in System Settings > Login Items. Or add a `slinger service install/uninstall` verb as a CLI path.
- (medium, M, verified) No app/daemon version handshake; updates leave a stale daemon running silently. control/src/wire.rs:11 has only protocol VERSION=1. The build sha reaches feedback notes only (daemon/src/feedback.rs:66). bundle.sh:6-7 says the running daemon keeps the old build. The workspace version is 0.0.0 (Cargo.toml:6), so every build shows the same version. Direction: Add a daemon_info verb that returns the version, build sha and exe path. Stamp the app too (share build.rs). On a mismatch, the app offers 'Restart slingerd' (a graceful stop verb, then respawn). Show both versions in an About panel. Stamp the sha into CFBundleVersion.
- (medium, S, likely) A daemon started outside a login shell cannot find claude. daemon/src/lib.rs:77-79: --claude defaults to a bare name looked up on PATH. claude is at ~/.local/bin/claude. A launchd or app-spawned process gets PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:..., so the first sling fails with processes.rs:82-84 'install Claude Code, or pass --claude'. Direction: Resolve the claude path once, in the core or daemon, from known locations (~/.local/bin, ~/.claude/local, the login-shell PATH), or from a config key. Report the resolved path in daemon_info. Any launcher depends on this fix.
- (medium, S, verified) Two install locations and a manual update/restart dance. bundle.sh:42-55 copies the app to /Applications and the binaries to ~/.local/bin as separate copies. Neither the daemon nor the app is restarted (bundle.sh:6-7). The steps that need a shell are build, PATH, start, restart on update, restart after a crash, --claude, plugin install and version check. Direction: Make the .app the single install: put the CLI and daemon inside it, and have --install symlink ~/.local/bin/{slinger,slingerd} into the bundle. Have `bundle.sh --install` (or `slinger update`) end by stopping the daemon gracefully and relaunching the app.
- (medium, S, speculative) Ad hoc signature likely invalidates macOS folder grants on every rebuild. bundle.sh:39 runs `codesign --sign -`. codesign -dv shows Signature=adhoc and TeamIdentifier not set. The privacy grants AGENTS.md ties to the bundle identity are most likely keyed to the cdhash for ad hoc apps (inferred, not tested). Direction: Sign with a stable local identity (a self-signed 'slinger dev' code-signing cert in the login keychain, its name passed by env var to bundle.sh), or a Developer ID if the app is distributed. Hand-check that the Downloads grant survives a reinstall.
- (low, S, verified) Bundle has no icon, so it shows a generic icon in the Dock and Spotlight. /Applications/slinger.app/Contents has no Resources directory. crates/app/Info.plist has no CFBundleIconFile. rg finds no icns in the repo. Direction: Add crates/app/slinger.icns, have bundle.sh copy it to Contents/Resources, and set CFBundleIconFile.
- (low, S, verified) Docs push service setup onto the user. docs/service.md:1233-1242 and README.md:31-41 tell the user to write their own service unit and run slingerd first. Direction: After the launcher work, rewrite these as one path ('open slinger.app') and keep the service-manager notes for headless or remote hosts.

Owner decisions (2026-11-20): slingerd outlives the app; the app spawns it when none answers; a login item comes later. One install location (binaries inside the .app, CLI symlinked) is accepted.

Source: 2026-11-20 audit.

title: switching and views: instant workspace switch, stable pane ids, views that come back
description:
[canvas-switch-perf] A switch is slow because of polling waits, not file IO. Real canvas files are small (largest is 449 KB), and the daemon keeps each canvas in memory after its first use. A sidebar tap only sets a mutex. The Watch thread sleeps 1 s before it reads the new workspace and fetches the layout. The main thread takes that news only on its 0.5 s tick. It then starts a new Follower, whose canvas_show reply also waits for the next tick. That adds up to about 0.5-2.0 s per switch (about 1.25 s on average), plus 0.5 s for PDF backdrops. While it waits, the pane keeps drawing the previous canvas, and the new canvas takes over the previous one's viewport because pane ids are reused. Nothing is cached, so switching back costs the same again. Recommendation: wake the main thread from the backend threads instead of polling, wake the Watch when a workspace is picked, store view state per workspace or canvas, and keep following every open workspace's canvas. Together these should cut a switch to about one frame. No builds were run, so the timings come from reading the code. Add the switch trace line described in the report to confirm them.
- (high, M, verified) Background news reaches the main thread only on the 0.5 s tick. platform/mod.rs:73 POLL_SECONDS=0.5; route.rs:81 returns Routed::News only for Tick, so other events skip news; main.rs:177-180 watch.layout and canvases.poll run only there; follow.rs:94 sends Shown into a channel with no wake. A switch waits for two ticks (layout, then Shown); PDFs wait for a third (canvases/pdf.rs:92). Direction: Give the backend a Wake handle that platform implements (performSelectorOnMainThread or a CFRunLoopSource). Follower, Watch, Pdfs and Outbox call it after a send, and the app dispatches a News event on the existing poll path. Keep the tick only for config stats and fades.
- (high, S, verified) Watch sleeps 1 s and ignores want(); layout waits behind UI and agent fetches. backend.rs:69 EVERY=1s; backend.rs:136-139 want() only sets a mutex; backend.rs:111-131 runs layout, load UIs (2 RTT plus a temp-file export each, backend/ui.rs:24-38) and workspaces() (session_list plus workspace_list) before it sends the layout, then sleeps. Direction: Wait on a Condvar with a timeout and have want() notify it. Send the layout before the UI and agent fetches. Better: start following the tapped workspace's canvas at once, since the sidebar already has Workspace.canvas.
- (high, S, verified) After a switch the pane shows the old canvas and keeps its viewport. panes.rs:53-62 rebuilds the Tree, so the first pane is always PaneId(0) (tree.rs:68-72). canvases.rs:427 keeps views keyed by PaneId. canvases.rs:445-455 draws view.last, the old canvas's scene, while the new mirror is None. The new canvas inherits the old pan and zoom. Direction: Key View by (workspace, pane number) or by (canvas, page), and drop last and the viewport when the pane's canvas changes. Show an empty or cached page instead of the old one. Store the viewport per canvas so a canvas opens the same way each time (the orientation issue).
- (medium, M, verified) No cache: every switch, including back, re-fetches and re-parses the page. canvases.rs:418 open.retain drops the Follower and Mirror of every canvas not shown; canvases.rs:419-426 starts a new Follower, which costs a canvas_show RTT, a JSON parse, Mirror::new and a tick. platform/web.rs:214-245 closes the UI WKWebViews of panes no longer shown, so they reload on return and lose their state. Direction: Keep following the canvases of all open workspaces (usually fewer than 10, one thread and one long poll each) or an LRU of them. A switch then re-renders with no round trip. Hide web views instead of closing them.
- (low, S, verified) Dropped followers stay blocked in the daemon for up to 25 s. follow.rs:22 WAIT=25s; follow.rs:71-74 Drop only sets a flag, so the thread stays in canvas_changes. server.rs:164-169 runs one daemon thread per connection, and feed.rs:43 blocks it. Fast switching piles up idle threads and sockets. Direction: Shut the stream down on Drop through a shared handle, or remove the churn by keeping followers alive as in finding 4.
- (low, S, verified) Per-show and per-second work grows with item, workspace and UI count. log.rs:320 serializes each page item to a String and parses it back. workspaces.rs:240-245,394-406: workspace_list re-reads every workspace file every second. backend/ui.rs:28-34 exports UI code through a temp dir on every layout change. All are cheap at today's sizes (the largest canvas is 449 KB, 1470 lines). Direction: Do this after findings 1-4: build each item's Value directly, cache workspace files by mtime, and return UI html inline from ui_shown.
- (medium, S, verified) No timing instrumentation for a switch. The only latency log is the pen's (SPEC O2, ink delay_log, main.rs:462). Nothing times the switch phases or the daemon's handling of a request, so these estimates come from reading the code. Direction: Behind SLINGER_TRACE=switch, log one line per switch with the time from the tap to each phase: watch read, layout sent, layout taken, Shown, Shown taken, first paint. Log the request kind, time and reply bytes in the daemon's converse.
- (low, S, verified) No key or palette command to switch workspaces. commands.rs:117-124,248-250 has only open, close and show-folder for workspaces. Switching works only by tapping the sidebar (window.rs:104). Direction: Add next-workspace, previous-workspace and cmd+1..9, routed through the same pick path as a sidebar tap.

[view-restore] The workspace keeps the pane arrangement (splits, ratios, what each pane shows). The daemon stores it in the project's slinger-workspace.toml and rewrites that file on every split, close and resize, and the arrangement does come back on reopen. The window frame, whether the sidebar is open, and the last workspace shown are saved in the app's macOS user defaults (NSUserDefaults). Nothing else is saved: pan and zoom, the page shown, focus, the stepped-into box and the reader scroll position all reset on every launch to page 1, 100%, top-left, pane 1. Per-pane view state is keyed by a pane id that comes from the pane's place in the tree, so it carries over between workspaces: a workspace switch gives the new canvas the old pane's zoom and scroll, and closing a pane shifts the other panes' views. The main recommendation is to give panes stable ids in the core layout. The daemon should then store per-pane views (page, pan and zoom, focus) in its data directory. Restore those views on reopen, use a content fit on first open, and copy the source pane's view on a split.
- (high, M, verified) Per-pane view keyed by positional PaneId leaks across workspace switch and shifts on pane close. panes.rs:53-62 rebuilds Tree::default each layout; tree.rs:33-38,68-72 ids by build order; canvases.rs:429 retains views by id only; reader.rs:18-29 leaves non-PDF viewport untouched; shared.rs:91 keeps focus number across switch Direction: Add stable pane ids to the core layout text and PaneTree (canvas:x@3, next id stored). Key app View and focus by (workspace, pane id), and drop views when the workspace changes.
- (high, L, verified) Viewport, page, focus, trail and reader scroll are never saved; every open is page 1 at 100% top-left. canvases.rs:133-150 View only in memory; layout.rs:104-107 Viewport::start; no viewport in core/control/daemon; SPEC.md:63 says client holds no durable state Direction: Core module workspace/view.rs owns per-(workspace,pane id) view; daemon stores it in data dir (not project/canvas file); pane_list returns it, new pane_view verb sets it, app sends debounced on pan/zoom end, page turn, quit.
- (medium, S, verified) First open ignores content; no zoom-to-fit or go-to-content command. layout.rs:104-107 start() fixed origin; paging.rs:52-54 only in/out/100%; registry.rs:77; only PDF canvases fit (scene/pdf.rs:95) Direction: Pure fit function in app layout (content bbox, min(100%,fit), 16pt margin) used when no stored view exists; expose as zoom-to-fit command.
- (medium, S, verified) Split opens the new pane on page 1 at start view instead of cloning the source pane. shared.rs:232-236 split via daemon then Panes::follow; canvases.rs:440-444 new id gets View::default (page None = first page, start viewport) Direction: On split, copy source pane's View (page, viewport, trail) to the new pane id; with stored views, daemon pane_open copies the view record.
- (medium, S, verified) Workspace switch waits for 1 s Watch poll; sidebar shows new workspace before panes follow. route.rs:85-95 only watch.want(name); backend.rs:69,129 thread sleeps EVERY=1s; backend.rs:117-121 fetches UI codes before telling layout Direction: On switch, fetch pane_list synchronously (or wake the watch via a channel) and apply it in the same step, as split/close already do; restore that workspace's views at once.
- (medium, M, verified) Every split/resize rewrites slinger-workspace.toml in the user's project root. daemon workspaces.rs:286-293 writes whole file per change; docs/workspace.md:9 file syncs with dir; this repo hides it via .git/info/exclude Direction: Keep pane contents in the workspace file if the owner wants it shared; move ratios and views to daemon data dir as per-machine view state.
- (low, M, verified) Two pane-tree implementations (core panes.rs and app layout/tree.rs). core workspace/panes.rs 381 lines and app layout/tree.rs+divider.rs 393 lines both do split/close/resize/MIN_RATIO/MAX_PANES; app split/close only used for no-workspace fallback (shared.rs:238) Direction: Shrink app tree to geometry over the control PaneTree (rects, divider hit, toward); let all structural changes go through the daemon.
- (low, S, likely) Startup draws a hard-coded canvas:main before the real layout arrives. shared.rs:61-65 default pane canvas main; main.rs:150 first view starts follower; user data dir has no main canvas Direction: Start with an empty 'opening' state (no follower) until the first layout reply, or fetch the layout synchronously before the first frame.
- (low, S, verified) SPEC says client holds no durable state but app persists frame, sidebar and workspace; bundle vs bare binary use different defaults domains. SPEC.md:63; platform/remember.rs:41-74 NSUserDefaults; defaults domains com.github.jayminwest.slinger vs slinger-app differ Direction: Amend SPEC: arrangement and views are the server's, window chrome is the app's. Optionally pin the defaults suite name so cargo run and the bundle share chrome state.

Owner decisions (2026-11-20): view state lives in the daemon; reopen restores the last view; first open fits the content.

Source: 2026-11-20 audit.

title: command targets: right-click menus, close from the sidebar, standard Mac menus
description:
[context-menus] The app has no secondary-click behaviour. platform/input.rs uses the right and middle buttons only to drag-pan (RIGHT, lines 111-124). A right click that does not drag does nothing. The Pen struct carries only the shift modifier, so a ctrl+click acts as a plain click. NSMenu is used only for the menu bar, but that code (platform/menu.rs made() and Target::run: -> Event::Command) can be reused as-is for a pop-up. Every registry command acts on implicit state: the focused pane, the selection, or the shown workspace. So a context menu has to make its target current first, or commands need an explicit subject. Recommendation: add a pure commands/context.rs that maps (Subject at the pointer, keymap) to Vec<Item>, the same Item type the menu bar uses. Add one pure enabled predicate that both menus share. The app's job is to resolve the subject and make it current, then return Step::Menu. The platform only pops up an NSMenu. Open the menu on right-mouse-up below a movement threshold, so right-drag still pans.
- (high, S, verified) No right-click/ctrl+click handling; right press only feeds a pan. platform/input.rs:111-124: RightMouseDown sets RIGHT and returns false; RightMouseUp clears it. No Event for a click. pen() at input.rs:228-235 reads only Shift; Pen (scene/ink.rs:71) has no ctrl bit. Direction: Add a ctrl bit (or mods) to Pen. In input.rs send Event::Context(at) on RightMouseUp when the pointer moved less than a slop, and on ctrl+LeftMouseDown that is not a tablet event. Right-drag past the slop stays a pan.
- (high, M, verified) Pure target->menu function from the registry; platform only pops NSMenu. commands/menu.rs:23-30 Item and bar() at l.197 are pure. platform/menu.rs:90 made() and Target::run: (l.39) already route a chosen item to Event::Command. The same command lists are hand-picked again in status.rs:174-255 and pages/menu.rs:47. Direction: Add commands/context.rs with items(subject, keymap, checked) -> Vec<Item>, unit-tested. The app adds subject_at(at) (built from taps, Dividers, pane_at, topmost) and returns Step::Menu(items, at, scene). Add platform/menu.rs pop() that reuses made().
- (medium, M, verified) Commands have no explicit subject, so a menu on a non-current target must switch focus first. window.rs:75-108 tap acts on shared.panes.focus(). close_workspace uses sidebar.close(), which closes the shown workspace (sidebar.rs:240). agent() and finder() use shown_dir(). RenamePage and RemovePage act on the shown page. Direction: Choose one: (a) make the target current first (focus the pane, select the item, show the workspace), which is cheap but triggers the slow workspace switch; or (b) Event::Command(Command, Option<Subject>), which lets 'Close' on any sidebar row work without switching.
- (medium, M, verified) Menu items are never disabled; no availability predicate. commands/menu.rs:23-30 Item has no enabled field. validate_menu_item (platform/mod.rs:263) judges only cut, copy and paste. Export UI, Fold and Step in show as enabled even when they cannot act, and the failure only flashes. Direction: Add a pure can(command, &AppState) -> bool and an Item.enabled field. Both the menu bar and the context menu use it, and the platform sets NSMenuItem enabled from it.
- (high, S, verified) Close/manage a workspace from its sidebar row is impossible. sidebar.rs:330: a row's only tap is Tap::Workspace(i) (or Run(StartAgent)). CloseWorkspace (cmd+alt+w) is reachable only from the File menu or the palette, and only for the shown workspace. Direction: Give the workspace row's context menu Show, Close workspace, Show folder in Finder, and Start/Stop/Restart agent. This depends on the explicit-subject decision above.
- (medium, S, likely) Web views and entry fields likely show their own native context menus. input.rs:111 returns false, so the right press goes on to AppKit. web.rs WKWebView sets no contextmenu or willOpenMenu handling (rg finds none), so WebKit's default menu (Reload, Back) probably appears on agent UIs and live items. entry.rs NSTextField shows the text menu. Direction: Hand-check this. Then suppress WebKit's menu (willOpenMenu or an injected contextmenu preventDefault) and show slinger's menu for the UI pane or live item (Export UI, Close pane, Delete, Sling). Keep the native menu in entry fields.
- (low, S, likely) Pen barrel button as right click becomes a pan, contradicting SPEC P4. SPEC.md:20 says 'A tablet button is a key'. input.rs reads no tablet subtype on Right events, so a Wacom side switch set to right click pans when dragged and does nothing when clicked. Direction: Treat a barrel right-click without a drag as Event::Context, as for a mouse. Update docs/design/pen-less.md:80-89 and SPEC P4 to say so. Add a check to hand-check seeds slinger-de037f and slinger-75514e.
- (low, S, verified) PageMenu is a second, private menu system with its own command titles. scene/pages/menu.rs:47-51 keeps its own COMMANDS titles ('Rename page…') beside Command::title(). It draws its own panel. window.rs:83-93 opens it from footer taps. Direction: Keep the drawn panel for pen taps, but take its command rows from context::items(Subject::Page), so titles and enabled state live in one place.

[close-workspace] Closing a workspace already works end to end. The daemon has Workspaces::close (workspaces.rs:333), the control verb is workspace_close, the CLI has `slinger workspace close`, and the app has close-workspace in the File menu and the palette with the default key cmd+alt+W (config.example.toml:260). The feature was added in b6bfcde, and the owner hand check (slinger-14fd9a) is still open. So the owner's "doesn't exist" means people can't find it. The sidebar, which is where workspaces are listed, shows no close control for a healthy workspace (only a broken one gets a "Close workspace" line). There is no right-click or ctrl-click menu, because the right button pans the canvas. Close also only acts on the workspace the window is showing. Two lifecycle bugs follow from the code: closing orphans a running agent that nothing can then stop, and opening a different folder with the same name silently takes over a closed workspace's canvas. Recommendation: give close a target and put it in the sidebar (a ✕ per row plus a context menu built from the pure commands::menu model). Move the agent and canvas-ownership rules into the daemon/core so close is safe. Add a recent list so a workspace can be reopened.
- (high, M, verified) Close-workspace exists but no healthy sidebar row has a close control, and there is no context menu. menu.rs:82, registry.rs:108, config.example.toml:260 (cmd+alt+w); sidebar targets are only row taps and broken/start lines (sidebar.rs:211-217,330; broken.rs:43-46); right-click is pan (platform/input.rs:111-124) Direction: Pure scene::sidebar adds a per-row ✕ (like the pane footer ✕) and a ctrl/right-click menu built from commands::menu; platform only shows the NSMenu. Consider cmd+shift+W as the default key.
- (high, S, likely) Closing a workspace orphans its running agent, which nothing can then stop. Workspaces::close only edits open.json (workspaces.rs:333-340); every session verb resolves the agent via workspaces().show (sessions.rs:154,204,243,276,321), which returns not_found after close; the session list covers only open workspaces (sessions.rs:326) Direction: Make the daemon decide in one place: close stops the workspace's agent process (or refuses with a hint while it runs). Document this in docs/service.md and the CHANGELOG.
- (medium, M, likely) Opening a new folder with a closed workspace's name silently adopts its canvas. canvas id = slug(name) (core/workspace.rs:198-213); open ignores a canvas Conflict (workspaces.rs:225-226) and checks uniqueness only against open workspaces (:208-220); canvases are stored flat in the data dir Direction: Core owns canvas ownership: a new workspace takes a free id (notes-2) when the canvas exists and is not its own, or the canvas lives beside the workspace folder.
- (medium, S, verified) Close takes no target and removes the sidebar row before the daemon answers. Sidebar::close uses self.at(), i.e. the shown workspace (sidebar.rs:240-244); Ask::Run carries no payload (route.rs:85-90); the row is removed before backend::close_workspace replies (window.rs:135-142) Direction: Route close as a tap carrying the workspace index or dir; Sidebar picks what shows next; remove the row only when the daemon reports success.
- (medium, M, verified) No reopen-recent: close forgets the workspace completely. workspaces/open.json holds only open dirs; close removes the dir (workspaces.rs:337); reopening needs the folder panel again Direction: Daemon keeps a recent/closed list in the same file and returns it in workspace_list; app adds File > Open Recent and a sidebar section.
- (medium, M, verified) No way to rename a workspace in any layer. the name is the TOML name field (core/workspace.rs:40-44), and tag defaults to the name; no verb in control, CLI or app Direction: Add workspace_rename via Workspaces::edit (workspaces.rs:308, which already rewrites the file atomically). Core keeps the canvas and tag stable. The app reuses the page-rename entry (scene/pages.rs:122).
- (medium, L, verified) Canvas lifecycle is missing everywhere: no delete or rename verb, and canvases pile up. No canvas_delete in the control Request enum (control/src/lib.rs:66-170); daemon Canvases has create/import/list/apply but no delete (canvases.rs); closed workspaces' .canvas files stay in the data dir Direction: Decide whether canvases belong strictly to a workspace (archived or deleted with it) or are first-class. The first is simpler; then add a forget/delete workspace verb.
- (low, S, verified) The sidebar is always alphabetical and cannot be reordered; after a close, the first in the list shows. list sorts by name (workspaces.rs:243); at() falls back to the first usable workspace (sidebar.rs:263-270), not the one used before Direction: Owner decides the order. open.json already keeps the open order, so serving it unsorted plus a move verb would allow manual order. After a close, show the most recently used workspace.
- (low, S, verified) A successful close gives no feedback and no way back. window.rs:135-142 flashes only on an error; how to reopen is written only in config.example.toml:257-259 and the CHANGELOG Direction: Flash 'Closed X · File > Open Recent' on success, once a recent list exists.

[menus-keys] The command system has a solid core. One dispatch path runs a menu key through the keymap, menu items show the live chord, and tests check that every command is in one menu and that no key sits on two items. The problems are macOS conformance and how the command data is organised. The app menu and Window menu are missing standard items: no Hide (so cmd+H does nothing), no Settings (cmd+,), no full-screen item or ctrl+cmd+F, and no Window list. The menu bar uses its own grouping, which does not match the registry Group that the palette and key overlay show. Each command's facts are spread over five hand-aligned tables, one of them an 85-slot positional keymap. Several default keys fight macOS conventions (cmd+J duplicate, cmd+N new page, cmd+shift+W/S/T pop-ups). Menu items are never disabled. There is no keyboard or palette way to switch workspaces or canvases. Close workspace does exist (opt+cmd+W in the File menu and in the palette), so the owner's complaint about it is a discoverability problem. Main recommendation: merge the commands into one table (name, title, menu, default chord, state) that the keymap, menu, palette, overlay and example config all derive from. Then do one convention pass on the keys and the menus.
- (high, S, verified) App/Window menus lack standard macOS items: Hide, Settings, Full Screen, Window list, Services. commands/menu.rs:77 app menu = About, Reload config, Quit; Native enum menu.rs:43-49 has only About/Cut/Copy/Paste/Minimise; no setWindowsMenu/setHelpMenu/hide:/toggleFullScreen: anywhere (rg). cmd+H reaches input.rs:97, unbound -> beep (inferred). No settings command in Command::ALL. Direction: Add Native Hide/HideOthers/ShowAll/Zoom/ToggleFullScreen/BringAllToFront and a Services submenu, a 'settings' command on cmd+, that opens config.toml (seeded from the example), and the title 'Quit slinger'. Register the Window and Help menus with AppKit. Keep the layout in commands::menu (pure).
- (medium, M, verified) Two taxonomies: registry Group (palette/overlay) vs menu BAR disagree. registry.rs:8 says Group is 'a menu in the menu bar' (also SPEC D21) but commands/menu.rs:76-193 BAR is independent. Undo/SelectAll/Find are Group::Canvas (registry.rs:167-199) but in the Edit menu; Pages are in the File menu; Quit and feedback are Group::Window but in the app and Help menus. Direction: Use one grouping. Make the menu the group (App, File, Edit, View, Agent, Pane, Window, Help) and have the palette and overlay headings read it, or derive BAR from Group plus an order. Fix the registry.rs doc comment.
- (medium, M, verified) A command's facts live in 5 hand-aligned tables; default keymap is positional. Enum commands.rs:18-186; names ALL :193-279 (hard-coded 85); Keymap::default is [Option<Chord>;85] matched to ALL by index :330-418; title and group are separate exhaustive matches in registry.rs:51-230; BAR is in menu.rs; comments are in config.example.toml:124+. Direction: Put one const Spec table in the registry: {command, name, title, menu, default:'cmd+d'}. Derive ALL, Keymap::default, title(), group() and the menu from it, and have a test compare it with config.example.toml. A new verb then needs one row.
- (medium, S, verified) Default chords clash with macOS/creative-app conventions. commands.rs:406 cmd+J duplicate (convention cmd+D, used here for split :339); :372 cmd+N new page; :385 cmd+O opens PDF while workspace is cmd+shift+O :387; :338 cmd+shift+W pick-width; :336 cmd+shift+S pick-shape; :380 cmd+shift+F feedback; :384 cmd+opt+R reveal; :349 cmd+B sidebar (macOS ctrl+cmd+S). Direction: Do one convention pass (SPEC O4 leaves the final keys open): cmd+N new workspace or canvas, cmd+O open workspace, cmd+shift+O import, cmd+D duplicate, split on cmd+\ and cmd+shift+\, sidebar on ctrl+cmd+S. Move the pop-ups off the cmd+shift letters that macOS owns.
- (high, M, verified) No commands or palette mode to switch workspace/canvas/page. Command::ALL (commands.rs:193-279) has no next/previous/go-to workspace or canvas and no new workspace (open-workspace makes the folder through the panel, :117-119). Palette rows come only from Command::ALL (scene/palette.rs:6-7). Switching is by sidebar tap only. Direction: Have the pure layer list the switch targets. Add a 'Go to…' palette mode (cmd+P) over workspaces, canvases and pages, plus next/previous-workspace commands. This addresses the 'switching is slow' complaint.
- (medium, M, verified) Menu items never disable; only the tool has a check mark. platform/menu.rs:36-55 Target answers only run:; window validateMenuItem covers only cut/copy/paste (platform/mod.rs ~261-272). Stop agent, Step out, Find next and Export UI are always enabled. Check mark only for the tool (commands/menu.rs:203); toggle-grid has none; 'Show or hide sidebar' is a static title (registry.rs:69). Direction: Add a pure Command::state(view) -> {enabled, checked, title} in the app's pure layer. The menu (validateMenuItem by tag) and the palette (dim unavailable rows) read it. Show dynamic Show/Hide Sidebar titles and a check mark on Dotted grid.
- (medium, S, verified) Close workspace exists but is hard to find (opt+cmd+W, deep in File). close-workspace returned in b6bfcde (slinger-c75719); bound to cmd+alt+w (commands.rs:388) and in the File menu (menu.rs:82). The owner reports that it 'doesn't exist in UI', so it is not discoverable. There is no right-click on a sidebar row (input.rs:110-122: right mouse pans). Direction: Add a close control on a hovered sidebar row and a sidebar context menu (Close, Show in Finder, Rename). Consider cmd+shift+W for close-workspace once pick-width moves.
- (low, S, verified) Menus are long flat lists: no separators or submenus. commands/menu.rs:22-30 Item has no separator. Edit has 26 items, 10 of them nudges or next-item that show no key because of the types() filter (:202). Tools has 23 items that mix tools, sizes, pop-ups, sling and agent lifecycle (:128-152). Direction: Add Item::Separator and submenus. Add an Agent menu (sling, dictate, start, stop, restart) and put pages in View or a Page menu. Drop the arrow nudges from the menu and keep them in the key overlay.
- (low, S, verified) Command titles break HIG style: case, ellipsis, spelling, verbs. registry.rs:51-138 uses sentence case ('Split right'). British 'Minimise' (menu.rs:58) and 'Pick a colour'. Ellipsis is uneven: 'Find text…' has one, but 'Rename page' and 'Sling selection' (both open a prompt) do not. Verbs drift: remove-page, delete-selection, close-pane, and 'Select', 'Select all', 'Select nothing'. Direction: Write one style rule in the docs (title case, an ellipsis on anything that asks for input, macOS standard names such as Minimize) and apply it in the single registry table.
- (low, S, verified) Window close quits app; cmd+W never closes the window. platform/mod.rs:275-280: closing the window terminates the app. cmd+W is close-pane and the last pane stays (commands.rs:33-34), so cmd+W does nothing when one pane is left. Direction: Owner decision. Option 1: cmd+W on the last pane closes the window, the app stays in the Dock and a Dock click reopens it. Option 2: keep quit-on-close but say so.

Owner decisions (2026-11-20): the context menu is a native NSMenu, opened on right-mouse-up so right-drag still pans.

Source: 2026-11-20 audit.

title: canvas library and storage: canvases as visible files in the workspace folder
description:
[storage-location] Canvases are stored as flat files at ~/Library/Application Support/slinger/canvases/<id>.canvas. Each workspace's slinger-workspace.toml sits in the user's folder, but the canvas it names does not, so syncing the folder (2 of the 3 open workspaces are under ~/sync) moves only the toml. Opening that folder on another machine silently creates an empty canvas with the same id. Size does not justify a database: the largest real canvas is 449 KB for 1467 imported strokes, and stroke point arrays make up 99.9% of it. Churn overhead on the hand-drawn canvas is about 2x. Canvas files are also not self-contained, because the PDF and live-UI blobs they reference live only in the machine-local record.sqlite. Recommendation: a hybrid. Canvases become visible documents in the workspace folder, the daemon resolves id to path through an index, referenced blobs travel with the canvas, the record and other machine state stay in App Support, and compaction is added later. Before any move there must be a single-writer guard on each canvas file.

[sidebar-nav] The sidebar lists only workspaces and agent status (SPEC D17). It is still the app's only navigator. Canvases are never listed: the app never calls canvas_list. A PDF or tldraw canvas has no way back once its pane closes, and reopening the file makes a `-2` copy. When you tap a workspace in the sidebar, the panes can take a second or more to change. In that time the sidebar and the panes disagree about which workspace is shown, so some commands act on one and some on the other. Close-workspace exists, but only in the menu bar, the palette and opt+cmd+W. It acts only on the shown workspace, does not ask first, and has no undo. Main recommendation: one pure navigation model (workspace → canvases → pages, with an explicit target per action), shown as a scrolling sidebar tree with per-row and right-click actions. A palette switcher would be the fast path. One owner should hold "the shown workspace", and the watch should wake as soon as you pick one.

title: perf: a synthetic 5 MB+ canvas fixture, and measure switch, sling and pen latency on it
description:
The owner's real canvases are 10-15x the largest on this machine and hold private data, so none can be copied here. Write a generator (a test helper or an xtask) that makes a canvas of realistic shape: thousands of strokes with long point arrays, several pages, text, boxes, a PDF item, edit churn. Then measure: workspace switch, canvas_show, a sling's packet and backdrop, pen-sample scene rebuild. Findings that grow with file size:
- Packets/backdrops replay entire op history 3x per call; sling does it twice. - Every packet and backdrop replays the whole op history three times, even though `Log` already holds the canvas. A sling does this twice. - Packets give ids by replaying ops that carry no ids, so any id gap in the file shifts them (correctness).
- route.rs:111 leads to window.rs:405 view(), then canvases.rs:435-490 for each pane: Ink::shown Vec plus HashSet of all items (ink/shown.rs:19-21), build_with over all items (scene/canvas.rs:237-260) smoothing each visible stroke again (:387), changed_between with 2 HashMaps and deep compare (:295-305). Mouse coalescing is off (mod.rs:375).

Direction: In the pure scene: cache each item's Draw in canvas coords per View, keyed by (ItemId, revision bumped by the Mirror). Rebuild only changed items, apply the viewport as an affine transform when painting (so a pan rebuilds nothing), and derive `changed` from the changed ids.

Direction: Keep the in-progress stroke's thinned, eased curves in Ink and append to them, recomputing only the last EASES+3 curves. Give the scene a borrowed mark and the tail box as `changed`. Add a test ratchet: per-point cost stays the same across a 2000-point stroke.

title: cleanup: one command table, typed verbs, Canvases split by concept, a short ARCHITECTURE.md
description:
Structural work for after the launcher, switching and command-target tracks land (they reshape the same code).

- [app-structure] Canvases is a god struct mixing view state, tools, features and IO actors. canvases.rs:69-123 ~28 fields; 20 files each `impl Canvases`, ~152 pub fns; canvases.rs:157-195 new() starts Outbox, Slinger, Lives, Pdfs, Noter, Flick; tests build it with fake socket (canvases/profile.rs:82) Direction: Split by state owner: Pages (followers+mirrors), PaneViews (viewport/page/trail), Gesture (ink/select/shapes/crop), feature modules (sling/feedback/dictation/find/fold/pdf) owning their actor handles. App owns them.
- [app-structure] Pane viewport keyed by tree slot leaks across workspace/canvas switches. views: Vec<(PaneId,View)> canvases.rs:71,135; PaneId = tree slot layout/tree.rs:30-43, rebuilt from root in panes.rs:53-62; retain by id canvases.rs:429; only page filtered by canvas (canvases/find.rs:51-58), viewport not reset Direction: Key view state by (workspace, pane, canvas) or reset View when shown canvas changes; one pure 'opening viewport' rule (fit/origin/remembered); optionally persist per canvas/page.
- [app-structure] Shown workspace owned in five places; selection rule duplicated. Sidebar.shown/last/at scene/sidebar.rs:97-101,263; backend/panes.rs:22-40 re-implements first-usable/last; Watch.wanted backend.rs:136; main `named` main.rs:153; Shared.workspace shared.rs:36; pick() returns None for unnamed but sets Dir (sidebar.rs:230-235) -> mismatch Direction: One pure Selection value resolving config name/tap/last/list to a dir+name; sidebar renders it, Watch receives the resolved name and never re-resolves.
- [app-structure] Workspace switch latency: 1 s unwoken poll plus 0.5 s ticks. want() only sets Mutex backend.rs:136-138; thread sleeps EVERY=1s backend.rs:69,129; Tick 0.5s platform/mod.rs:73; new Follower started in show() canvases.rs:419-425, first page on next tick Direction: Wake Watch on want() (condvar/recv_timeout); post an event to the run loop when news arrives instead of draining on a timer; keep recently shown canvases' followers warm (small LRU).
- [control-protocol] App binary-size ratchet shapes the protocol and blocked user-visible features (close workspace). budgets/binary-size-budget.json: 1572864, raised 4x (git log). Seed slinger-c75719 shows close-workspace was reverted in d35bc18 because of the budget; 5f4959, dd0783, 99061d, c57a12 were also held back by it. Size comments at lib.rs:118,166; workspace.rs:1-6; client.rs:216 canvas_import_id; docs/app-parity.md:22-28 Direction: Owner decides: replace the ceiling with a coarse sanity cap, or keep it but stop letting it shape the wire types. Treat app parity as the ratchet instead.
- [control-protocol] Verbs declared 3 ways; a new verb touches ~9 places; request-reply pairing untyped. lib.rs:66-117 has serializable variants; lib.rs:121-163 has skip_serializing variants with mirror types (workspace.rs:18, look.rs:21, find.rs:16, feed.rs:24, packet.rs:19); lib.rs:170-198 has untagged groups. Reply is untagged (lib.rs:203). client.rs:285 deserializes any T. No test checks service.md's verb table Direction: Use one pattern: a tagged XAsk enum per module. Add a trait Verb{const OP; type Reply} and a generic Client::call<V>. Drop the Reply enum and the mirror types. Add a test that the ops listed in code match the service.md table both ways.
- [architecture-drift] App re-implements core rules (hit tests, fold, text cell, canvas codec) with no parity check. app scene/select/hit.rs:1-6 'core's rules... kept here as well... Keep the two alike'; mirror/fold.rs:1-8; glyphs.rs:44 CELL=0.5 dup of core render/mod.rs:126; mirror.rs:347-448 + mirror/write.rs:289-320 hand JSON codec. layer-rules app-uses-the-socket bans slinger_core even in tests. Direction: Extract a pure IO-free model crate (items, file-object codec, geometry, fold holders, text frame) that core re-exports and app/control link; or add shared golden fixtures that core writes and app tests read.
- [architecture-drift] ARCHITECTURE.md is a 1462-line per-file narrative, not a map. App section 379-1343 (811-line code fence 381-1192: key bindings, pixel offsets); Boundaries table 1355-1440 ~85 rows, ~10 real boundaries; changed in 351/1011 commits in 10 days. Direction: Cut to ~200 lines: layer diagram, one-request path, per-crate top-module map with the decision each hides, app data flow, ~10 gate-held boundaries, known-duplicates list, Adding things. Move behaviour to module rustdoc/docs/design.
- [size-budget-pressure] Canvases: one 28-field struct whose impl is spread over 21 files. canvases.rs:69-125 has 28 fields; `impl Canvases` is in canvases.rs plus 20 child files with about 150 fns. Fields each file uses: paging.rs 10, sling.rs 10, seek.rs 9, drag.rs 9, slung.rs 9. The mod declarations are in two blocks (22-35, 61-66). Splits came from line counts (slinger-5d6ede, 57de033). Direction: Make Canvases a coordinator over 3-4 sub-structs that each own their state: Follow (open, views, turning, lives, pdfs, folds, steps), Editing (ink, select, shapes, crop, outbox, kept, pen), SlingFlow (sling, slinger, slung, prompt, voice, agents). Migrate one per commit.
- [size-budget-pressure] main/route/window: event routing split by line count, with an import cycle. window.rs:7-8 says it was 'Split from main.rs' and holds 20 unrelated free fns (39-484). route.rs:19 imports private Ask, asked and pen from main.rs (309, 335, 390), and main.rs calls route. These came from seed 72b81d and commits 3b30cb2, 4f3216c, ba2ffde. Direction: Keep main.rs to startup only. One events module owns Ask, ask, route and the pen/pointer dispatch. Workspace verbs (open/close/agent/finder) go to their own module. Pane geometry (pane_at, focus, divider) goes to panes/layout, and view() to scene.
- [size-budget-pressure] Binary-size budget drives feature reverts and distorted code, and is raised anyway. Ceiling went 393216 -> 1572864 in 4 raises (f44e5a5, 0e1e91b, db62ac7, 6ecad1c). Reverts: close-workspace (d35bc18), profile menu (629535f). Byte-driven code: HashMap->sorted list (19f91af), hand-rolled float parse (config/widths.rs:4-5), app-parity.md:21-26 and 95-104 track bytes per feature. Direction: Owner decision. Either replace the hard gate with a reported number, or keep a generous ceiling with the rule that features are never reverted for bytes. Then remove the hand-rolled parsers and the byte accounting from the docs.
- [terminology] 'session' vs 'agent' vs 'conversation': one concept, three words; session also means 3 things. cli/src/session.rs:25-37 (session start <WORKSPACE>, show <AGENT>, --fresh 'new session'); registry.rs:110-112 'Start agent'/'Restart agent in a new conversation'; backend/ui.rs:57 'start its session'; scene/slung.rs:417 'Claude Code session'; core/session.rs:113 Direction: User-facing noun 'agent' (CLI agent list/show/start/stop/send/listen, keep session as alias). Call Claude's resumable transcript a 'conversation'. Core Session stays, documented as the daemon's entry for one agent.
- [terminology] 'box' is both an item kind and geometry (--box flags, 'its box' output). item.rs:229 Shape::Box (fold container); put.rs:24 --box W,H makes a box; edit.rs:24-28 --box resizes any item; packet.md:368 crop --box x,y,w,h region; guide 'prints id and its box'; put.rs:35 --at 'corner of its box' Direction: Use 'box' only for the item kind. Geometry is 'frame' (core already uses frame: Rect). Add edit --size and crop --region, keep --box as an alias, and say 'frame' in output and help.
- [menus-keys] Each command's facts are spread over five hand-aligned tables, one of them an 85-slot positional keymap

Also undo the hand-rolled code that existed only for the binary-size budget (removed 2026-11-20): by-hand parsing and formatting in crates/app/src/{ui.rs:54, commands/registry.rs:260, commands/chord.rs:71, config/canvas.rs:26, config/widths.rs:6}, and the requests the app never sends for size reasons in crates/control/src/{packet,look,find,feed,workspace,client,lib}.rs and docs/service.md:1166 (ARCHITECTURE.md:655 too). The file-size cap stays at 500 lines (owner decision); splits follow concepts.

daemon: --log <FILE> for slingerd's and its agents' stderr; SIGHUP no longer ends it
description:
Why: a slingerd nobody started from a terminal has nowhere to write (its stderr is its only log: lib.rs:148, canvases.rs warnings; agents inherit it, processes.rs:208-209), and it traps only SIGTERM and SIGINT (crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:215), so a closed terminal kills it.
Add:
- Flag `--log <PATH>` on slingerd (crates/daemon/src/lib.rs Args). With it, before serving: make the parent directory; if the file is over 1 MiB rename it to `<PATH>.1` (replacing the old one); open it for append; point fd 2 at it (rustix, already a dependency; safe API such as rustix::stdio::dup2_stderr), so the daemon's warnings and every agent's stderr land there. Without the flag nothing changes (stderr as today).
- With --log only, one line at start: `<local time> slingerd <version> (<build>) pid <pid>: serving <data dir> on <socket>`, and one at a clean stop. The "says nothing on success" contract on a terminal stays.
- SIGHUP is ignored (signal-hook: register it so the default action is replaced). SIGTERM and SIGINT stop as today.
Constraints: the fd redirect must happen only in the slingerd binary (crates/daemon/src/main.rs), never inside `daemon::run` when tests call it in-process (it would redirect the test runner's stderr): e.g. main asks the library for the parsed log path, or passes a hook. Put the code in a new crates/daemon/src/log.rs; the pure parts (rotate-or-not by size, the line format) are functions with unit tests. No unsafe (layer rule platform-owns-ffi).
Tests: unit tests in log.rs; crates/daemon/tests/stderr.rs or signals.rs (they run the real binary, with its own --socket, a --data-dir in a tempdir and --scratch): with --log, a stand-in claude that writes to stderr shows up in the file, and so does a "workspace not loaded" warning; a file over the limit is rotated at start; after SIGHUP the daemon still answers, then SIGTERM exits 0.
Docs in the same commit: docs/service.md "The daemon" (synopsis, the flag, SIGHUP), ARCHITECTURE.md "Inside the daemon", CHANGELOG under Unreleased.

title: daemon: find Claude Code without PATH when --claude is not given
description:
Why: `--claude` defaults to the bare name `claude` (crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:78, store.rs:60), looked up on the daemon's PATH at spawn (processes.rs:194). A slingerd started by the app gets launchd's PATH (/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin); Claude Code is usually in ~/.local/bin. The first sling then fails with "install Claude Code, or pass its path with 'slingerd --claude <PATH>'" (processes.rs:82-84). No login shell is to be run for this (owner decision).
Add (new file crates/daemon/src/processes/program.rs; processes.rs is 445 lines, do not grow it past 500):
- `--claude` becomes optional. Given: used as written, as today. Not given: at each session start (not once at startup, so an install made later is found) take the first of these that is an executable file: `claude` in each folder of the daemon's PATH, then ~/.local/bin/claude, ~/.claude/local/claude, /opt/homebrew/bin/claude, /usr/local/bin/claude, ~/.nix-profile/bin/claude, /etc/profiles/per-user/<user>/bin/claude. Keep the list in one const.
- Pure functions with unit tests: `candidates(path: Option<&OsStr>, home: Option<&Path>, user: Option<&str>) -> Vec<PathBuf>` (order, empty PATH entries dropped, no HOME) and the pick over an injected "is executable" check. The environment is read once in `run` and passed in as a value: tests must not set process environment variables (they run in parallel).
- None found: a typed error, code `not_found`, message naming that Claude Code was not found and the places searched, hint "install Claude Code, or start slingerd with --claude <PATH>".
- `Processes` exposes the path it would run now (`Option<PathBuf>`), for the daemon_info verb of a later step.
Tests: unit tests above; crates/daemon/src/tests/process.rs through a real socket: with a search whose PATH lacks claude and whose home holds .local/bin/claude (the stand-in script the tests already write), a session starts; with none, session start fails `not_found` with the hint; an explicit --claude still wins.
Docs in the same commit: docs/service.md "The daemon" (--claude default) and "Sessions" where it names the program; ARCHITECTURE.md "Inside the daemon"; CHANGELOG.
Hand check (one line in docs/hand-check.md, under a heading "## Launcher (plan <this plan id>)", not a step): from a slingerd started by the bundled app, start an agent and sling once: Claude Code is found, its hooks report, its Bash tool finds git/cargo/sd, its MCP servers load (the agent inherits launchd's short PATH).

At start the daemon reads the PATH of the user's login shell once (run $SHELL -l -c with a short timeout, never per sling), falls back to fixed folders (~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, the nix profile dirs) joined with its own PATH, and uses that one PATH both to find claude and as the PATH it hands every agent process (processes.rs path_first). Keep this in one module with tests on the merge and the fallback; daemon_info reports the resolved claude path and PATH. This widens the step beyond the claude lookup.

title: control: one build stamp that the daemon, the CLI and the app all carry
description:
Why: only slingerd is stamped with its commit (crates/daemon/build.rs sets SLINGER_BUILD_SHA and SLINGER_BUILD_DIRTY; used in crates/daemon/src/feedback.rs:66 through slinger_core::feedback::build, crates/core/src/feedback.rs:225). The app must compare its own build with the daemon's, and it may not link the core (layer rule app-uses-the-socket). Every binary links slinger-control.
Do:
- Move crates/daemon/build.rs to crates/control/build.rs unchanged in behaviour (a value already in the environment wins; no git: nothing set; the rerun-if-changed list; the `../..` root still holds from crates/control). Remove the daemon's build script.
- New crates/control/src/build.rs: `pub fn stamp() -> String` (the sha in lowercase, `-dirty` after it, `dev` with no sha: exactly today's text) over a pure `text(sha: Option<&str>, dirty: Option<&str>)`, and `pub const PACKAGE: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`. Move the formatter and its tests out of crates/core/src/feedback.rs; the daemon's feedback.rs calls control's. Do not name anything `VERSION`: control already exports the protocol's `VERSION`.
- Leave `SLINGER_BUILD_SOURCE` and `feedback::default_file` (crates/daemon/src/feedback.rs:16-19, 139-143) as they are.
- crates/control/src/lib.rs is 477 lines: add only the `mod` and the `pub use`.
Behaviour that must not change: the `build` field of feedback notes; `slinger --version` and `slingerd --version` print the package version.
Tests: the moved unit tests in control; crates/daemon/tests/feedback.rs and crates/daemon/src/tests/feedback.rs still pass untouched (they hold the note's build text).
Docs in the same commit: ARCHITECTURE.md lines about build.rs and SLINGER_BUILD_SHA (around 347-348) and the layer text of crates/control.
Known limit, to state in the doc comment: two builds from the same commit with different uncommitted changes carry the same stamp.

title: verbs daemon_info and daemon_stop: control, daemon, and `slinger daemon info|stop`
description:
Why: the protocol has one integer VERSION (crates/control/src/wire.rs:11) and no request says which build answers, so an updated app cannot tell that an old daemon still runs; and the only way to stop a daemon is to find its pid.
Follow "Adding a verb" in docs/service.md. Step 1 there (the core) does not apply: these verbs describe the daemon's process, which the core cannot know (core-is-pure forbids std::env and std::process). Say so in the commit message.
- control: new crates/control/src/daemon.rs. `DaemonAsk` tagged by `op` (`daemon_info`, `daemon_stop`), read through one `Request::Daemon` variant marked `#[serde(untagged, skip_serializing)]` as crates/control/src/session.rs does, with the test that the ask writes the line `Request` reads. Replies: `DaemonInfo { version, build, protocol, pid, started_ms, exe, socket, data_dir, claude: Option<String>, slinger, log: Option<String> }` (version = build::PACKAGE, build = build::stamp(), claude = the path it would run now or null, log = the --log path or null) and `DaemonStopped { pid }`. Typed `Client::daemon_info()` and `Client::daemon_stop()`. lib.rs is 477 lines: add only the mod, the pub use and the two variants; move something out by concept if it would pass 500.
- daemon: new crates/daemon/src/server/daemon.rs and one arm in `answer` (crates/daemon/src/server.rs, 474 lines). `daemon_stop` replies, then stops exactly as SIGTERM does (`Stopper::stop`: replies already owed still go out, agents end, socket file and socket name removed, exit 0). The handler needs the Stopper and the facts `serve` knows (log path, start time): carry them on the Store or pass them to `converse`; no globals.
- CLI: new crates/cli/src/daemon.rs: `slinger daemon info` (text and --json per docs/cli.md) and `slinger daemon stop` (says nothing on success). Add both to the table in docs/cli.md; run the tests in crates/cli/src/tests/guide.rs and update the guide's command list if it is generated from the commands.
- docs/service.md: both verbs in the verb table with a short "The daemon's own verbs" section; under "Versioning" say that `v` stays 1 and that a daemon older than these verbs answers `bad_request`, which a client reads as "older build". docs/app-parity.md: one row for the two commands naming the later app step (the restart offer). ARCHITECTURE.md: "Inside the daemon" and one row in the Boundaries table. CHANGELOG.
Tests: control wire tests; a new crates/daemon/src/tests/daemon.rs through a real socket: every info field (pid is this process, socket and data_dir are the ones served, claude follows the search of the earlier step); a request made before the stop still gets its reply; after `daemon_stop` serve returns and the socket file is gone. crates/daemon/tests/signals.rs with the real binary: `daemon_stop` exits 0 and takes the socket name back. CLI tests in crates/cli/src/tests for both commands, text and --json.

title: bundle: slingerd and slinger inside slinger.app; --install symlinks the CLI into ~/.local/bin
description:
Why: scripts/bundle.sh puts only slinger-app in the bundle (lines 29-35) and --install copies slingerd and slinger to ~/.local/bin as separate files (42-52): two install locations that drift. Owner decision: one location, the binaries inside the .app, the CLI symlinked.
Change scripts/bundle.sh:
- Always build the three release binaries. Copy slingerd and slinger to Contents/MacOS beside slinger-app. This path is a contract the app step relies on: `<bundle>/Contents/MacOS/slingerd`.
- Sign the two helpers ad hoc first, then the bundle, then `codesign --verify --strict` the bundle; fail loudly (✗ line, non-zero exit) if a binary is missing or the check fails.
- crates/app/Info.plist: CFBundleVersion becomes `@BUILD@`, filled with the commit count (`git rev-list --count HEAD`, an integer that grows; the package version when there is no git). CFBundleShortVersionString stays `@VERSION@`. Pass SLINGER_BUILD_SHA through untouched so all three binaries carry one stamp.
- --install: copy the app to SLINGER_APP_DIR (default /Applications) as today (remove, then copy); then for slinger and slingerd remove whatever is at SLINGER_BIN_DIR/<name> (a file from an older install, or a link) and make a symlink to the binary inside the installed app. It stops and restarts nothing: the app offers that (a later step). Print the app's path as today.
- Rewrite the header comment (lines 2-12): it says the app neither ships nor starts slingerd.

title: app: start the bundled slingerd when none answers; show 'Starting slingerd…', not a shell hint
description:
Why: with no daemon the window is dead and shows `✗ slingerd does not answer on <socket>` with the hint `start it with 'slingerd --socket …'` (crates/control/src/client.rs:306-310) in the focused pane (scene.rs:211-216), the message again in the sidebar (scene/sidebar.rs:169-172, 281-284), and once per canvas follower (backend/follow.rs:85-89). Owner decisions: the app starts the bundled slingerd when none answers; slingerd outlives the app.
Pure decisions (new crates/app/src/launch.rs, unit tests with a passed-in clock, no IO):
- `bundled(exe: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf>`: `<X>.app/Contents/MacOS/slingerd` when exe is `<X>.app/Contents/MacOS/slinger-app`; None for a bare binary (target/debug/slinger-app, cargo run, tests). A bare binary never starts a daemon.
- Managed only when: there is a bundled slingerd that is a file, the config sets no `[daemon] socket`, the default data directory is known, and the app is not in --preview. Not managed: exactly today's behaviour.
- A state machine: Up; Down -> spawn -> Starting{since}; Starting -> Up when the socket answers; the child exiting 4 (another slingerd holds the lock: the race) is not a failure, keep waiting; any other exit, or 10 s with no answer -> Failed{why}; Failed tries again after 30 s; Up -> Down when the socket stops answering (a daemon that died is started again). One child at a time. "Down" means a connect to the app's socket (Settings::socket) is refused or the file is missing; a daemon that accepts but answers slowly is running (slinger-2f9883) and is never Down.
- What to show per state: Starting = one line "Starting slingerd…" in the muted colour, no ✗, no hint; Failed = "✗ slingerd did not start" with the exit code if any, hint "see <log path>".
IO (new crates/app/src/backend/daemon.rs; first move `Watch` out of crates/app/src/backend.rs, 497 lines, into backend/watch.rs as a pure move): a thread that checks the socket about once a second, runs the state machine, and on spawn runs `<bundle>/Contents/MacOS/slingerd --log <default data dir>/slingerd.log` with no --socket and no --data-dir (the defaults; never --scratch), stdin, stdout and stderr null, in its own process group (std CommandExt::process_group(0)) so it outlives the app; a thread waits on the child to reap it and report its exit code. The spawn is behind a small trait or closure so tests replace it. The app sends nothing to the daemon when it quits.
Window: while Starting or Failed, the launch line replaces the daemon-unreachable problems in the focused pane (shared.trouble and the followers' problems; a config problem still shows) and the sidebar's ✗ line; the Save flash says "Not saved yet: slingerd is starting". Decide in scene (a new scene/daemon.rs or in scene/sidebar), draw with the existing labels: no new platform code. main.rs (473), window.rs (495), scene.rs (496) and scene/sidebar.rs (470) are at the 500-line cap: put new code in new modules and move code out by concept where needed.
Tests: launch.rs table tests for every transition above and for `bundled`; scene tests: Starting shows the one muted line and no ✗ in pane and sidebar, Failed shows ✗ and the log hint, not managed shows today's text; backend/daemon.rs tests: a stub program proves the argv and that exit 4 and exit 1 are reported apart; with a spawner that serves the daemon library in-process (the app dev-depends on slingerd) on a tempdir socket and data directory, the state reaches Up and the Watch gets workspaces. No test starts a real slingerd binary on the default data directory.
Docs in the same commit: docs/service.md "Socket" (the bullet "The app finds the daemon the same way": add that the bundled app starts one); ARCHITECTURE.md "Inside the app" and a Boundaries row (a bare slinger-app never starts a daemon: held by the launch.rs tests); AGENTS.md conventions: opening a bundle starts a daemon on the default data directory when none runs, so to hand-check a bundle against a scratch daemon give it a config (SLINGER_CONFIG) whose `[daemon] socket` names that daemon; CHANGELOG.
