title: app: notice a slingerd of another build and offer to restart it; 'Restart slingerd' command
description:
Why: after an update the old daemon keeps running (scripts/bundle.sh header: "keeps the old build until it is restarted") and nothing says so. Stopping slingerd ends its agents' processes (docs/service.md "Clean stop"), so the app asks; it never restarts by itself.
Pure (crates/app/src/launch.rs or a sibling, unit tests): `skew(mine, theirs) -> Same | Differs { daemon: String } | Old`: Same when `version` and `build` of `daemon_info` equal the app's own `control::build::PACKAGE` and `control::build::stamp()`; Old when the daemon answers `bad_request` to `daemon_info` (it predates the verb); an unreachable daemon is no answer, ask again later. The offer exists only when the app is managed (it has a bundled slingerd to start, and no `[daemon] socket`).
Backend (crates/app/src/backend/daemon.rs): ask `daemon_info` each time the state turns Up and each time the socket changes; publish the skew with the daemon's pid.

title: app: a timing trace line for a workspace switch (SLINGER_TRACE=switch)
description:
Goal: one stderr line per workspace switch that shows where the time goes, so the audit's timings (read from code, never measured) are confirmed before and after the next steps. It goes first on purpose: it gives the baseline.

Behaviour: with the environment variable SLINGER_TRACE containing "switch" (read once in crates/app/src/main.rs; unset means no cost and no output), a pick of another workspace (sidebar tap, open-workspace, the config's workspace changing: every place that calls Watch::want) starts a trace. It prints one line when the first scene is drawn in which every canvas pane of the new layout has its page, for example: "switch notes: watch +612ms, layout +640ms, taken +1000ms, shown +1004ms, heard +1500ms, drawn +1512ms". Phases, each a time since the pick: watch (the Watch thread read the wanted name), layout (the Watch sent the layout), taken (the main thread took the layout), shown (a Follower got its canvas_show reply; the last one of the new panes), heard (the main thread took that News::Shown in Canvases::poll), drawn (the scene was handed to the platform). A new pick before the line is printed replaces the trace. A layout with no canvas pane prints at "taken".

Where: a new pure module crates/app/src/trace.rs owns the phases and the line's text (no IO; main.rs writes the line to stderr, as it does the pen's delay log at main.rs:460-466). The Watch thread (crates/app/src/backend.rs:105-133) stamps "watch" and "layout" with Instant and sends them with the layout; the Follower (crates/app/src/backend/follow.rs:91-94) stamps the time of its Shown. backend.rs is 497 lines and the cap is 500: first move Watch, load and tell, with their tests, to crates/app/src/backend/watch.rs (a pure move, re-exported from backend), then add the stamps. main.rs is 473 lines: keep the wiring short or move the news-taking part of the step closure to its own function.

A test with the real daemon helper (backend::tests::with_daemon, crates/app/src/backend/testing.rs) that a Watch's layout carries its two stamps in order and a Follower's Shown carries one.

title: app: backend threads wake the main thread, so news does not wait for the 0.5 s tick
description:
Problem (verified): news from every backend thread reaches the window only on Event::Tick, every POLL_SECONDS = 0.5 (crates/app/src/platform/mod.rs:73,237,378; crates/app/src/route.rs:79; main.rs:177-182). A switch pays two ticks (layout, then News::Shown), a PDF backdrop a third (canvases/pdf.rs:92).

Add:
1. crates/app/src/backend/wake.rs, pure. Wake is Clone + Send + Sync. Wake::new(post) wraps a function that asks the main thread to look; Wake::none() does nothing (tests, preview). wake() calls post unless a wake is already pending; taken() clears the pending mark. wake.channel::<T>() returns (Teller<T>, Receiver<T>); Teller::send sends and then wakes, so no thread can send news and forget to wake.
2. Every backend thread makes its news channel with wake.channel(): Watch (three channels), Follower (backend/follow.rs), Outbox (backend/outbox.rs), Slinger (backend/sling.rs), feedback (backend/feedback.rs), Flick (backend/flick.rs), Lives (canvases/live.rs), Pdfs and the open-pdf thread (canvases/pdf.rs). Pass the Wake through Watch::start and Canvases::new (or a builder beside Canvases::rendering); Canvases::reconnect keeps it.
3. platform: a new Event::Wake and a safe function platform::waker() that returns the post function. It may be called from any thread and makes the main run loop dispatch Event::Wake, in the common run-loop modes so it arrives during a pen stroke or a divider drag as the timer does (chrome.rs:60-72). Use what the crate already links (block2, objc2-foundation); platform only translates. platform/mod.rs is 498 lines: move Event and Step to crates/app/src/platform/event.rs (re-exported) in this step.
4. route.rs: Event::Wake takes the same path as Event::Tick (Routed::News(false)). In main.rs the news path calls wake.taken() before it drains the channels, so a send that races the drain posts again. The preview window's answer (main.rs:126) treats Wake as Tick.

The tick stays, as a clock only: it stats the config files, fades the flash and the sidebar notice, ticks the sling pill, retries a missed PDF, and it is the backstop for a wake that came while the answer was running (dispatch drops such an event: platform/mod.rs:303-304; this is why the pending mark is cleared on the main thread and not by the sender). Say so in the comment on POLL_SECONDS.

Keep the trace line of step 1 working: "taken" and "heard" now follow "layout" and "shown" by milliseconds.

Tests: wake.rs units (two wakes post once; after taken() the next wake posts; Teller::send wakes after the value is in the channel; none() is silent). follow.rs with the real daemon: a Follower given a counting Wake posts for Shown and for a change. route test: Event::Wake returns Routed::News. Every existing test passes Wake::none().

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (main.rs and backend.rs rows near lines 382-442, the threading and config paragraphs near 1198-1208, platform row, layer table if a boundary moves); the module comments of backend/follow.rs and platform/mod.rs; CHANGELOG under Unreleased, Changed: what an agent draws and a workspace switch show at once.

description:

1. The thread waits on a Condvar paired with the wanted workspace, with EVERY as the timeout. want() and Watch::follow(socket) set their value and notify, so the next round starts at once. title: core, control, daemon, CLI: stable pane ids in the workspace layout (layout version 2)
description:
Problem (verified): a pane has no identity. The layout text is "row 0.5 canvas:a ui:b" (crates/core/src/workspace/panes.rs:1-11) and a pane is named by a number that moves when panes open and close (docs/service.md "Panes"). The app can only key its per-pane state by position, which is the root of the view leaks.

Core (crates/core/src/workspace/panes.rs, 381 lines; move the text reading and writing to workspace/panes/text.rs if the file would pass 500):
- Each pane has an id: a u32 of 1 or more, unique in its layout, never given again in that layout. Layout keeps the next id. Layout::new gives id 1. Layout::open gives the new pane the next id. close and resize leave every other id as it was.
- Layout text version 2 (panes::VERSION = 2): a pane's word is "canvas:main@3"; the [layout] table holds version = 2, panes = "<text>" and next = <n>.
- Reading never fails for an id reason: version 1 text (no ids) gets 1..n in order; in version 2 a word with no id, a 0, or an id already used gets a fresh id; a missing or too-small next becomes the highest id + 1.
- Workspace::panes (crates/core/src/workspace.rs:271-280) reads versions 1 and 2; set_panes (285-290) writes version 2 and next, and keeps the table's other fields as it does today. A version 1 file is rewritten only by the first change to its panes; until then its ids are 1..n by position, which is what that write stores.
- Pane::word() for the record's pane_moved stays "canvas:notes", with no id: the record's contract does not change.

Control (crates/control/src/pane.rs): Pane gets "id" (#[serde(default)], so a reply from an older daemon reads as 0). The pane verbs still name a pane by its number.

Daemon (crates/daemon/src/server/pane.rs wire()): fill the id. CLI: 'slinger pane list --json' carries the id through serde; the text lines stay number, kind, target.

Tests: core panes tests (close the first of "row A B": B keeps its id; an id is not reused after close, also across encode and decode; version 1 text reads as 1..n and writes as version 2; missing, zero and duplicate ids are repaired; next is repaired; round trip). core workspace tests (a version 1 file read, changed and written as version 2 with next; other [layout] fields kept; a version 3 layout still falls back to one pane). control wire-line tests with and without id. daemon tests/pane.rs through the socket (ids stay across open, close and resize, and across a daemon restart on the same data directory). CLI test: the JSON has id.

Docs, same commit: docs/workspace.md "[layout]" (version 2, the id, next, what an older slingerd does with it: it shows one pane and replaces the layout at its next pane change, the rule already at docs/workspace.md:84-86); docs/service.md "Panes" (the id in the tree, numbers still name panes); ARCHITECTURE.md; docs/cli.md pane list JSON; CHANGELOG, Changed. crates/cli/src/guide.md only if it shows pane JSON.

title: app: key panes by the server's ids; views and focus per workspace; no old canvas in a new pane
description:
Problem (verified): Panes::follow builds a fresh Tree whose first pane is always PaneId(0) (crates/app/src/panes.rs:53-62, layout/tree.rs:68-72). Canvases keeps views by PaneId alone (canvases.rs:72,429). So after a workspace switch the new canvas gets the old pane's pan and zoom and the pane draws view.last, the old canvas's scene, until the new page comes (canvases.rs:448-457); closing the first of two panes gives the second the first's view; Shared::follow keeps the focus number across workspaces (shared.rs:91).

Change:
1. Panes::follow gives each pane the PaneId of its server id (control Pane.id from the step before). Tree needs a way to split with a given id; its own counter starts above the highest id, for the window's own splits when there is no workspace. A layout whose ids are 0 (an older daemon) falls back to today's build-order ids. crates/app/src/layout/ has a 100% line-coverage floor (budgets/coverage-budgets.json): test every new line.
2. Move View and its bookkeeping out of canvases.rs (497 lines) into crates/app/src/canvases/view.rs. A View knows the canvas it is for. When its pane shows another canvas, the view starts again (start viewport, first page, nothing drawn, no reader column, no trail).
3. Views are per workspace. Canvases learns the workspace the panes are for (an argument of Canvases::show or a field of Panes; take the smaller change) and, when it changes, parks the views under the old name and brings back those parked under the new one. Parked views are pruned to the layout's ids the next time their workspace is shown. No workspace (no daemon) is one more key.
4. A pane whose page has not come draws nothing of another canvas: an empty paper scene, or no scene, never view.last of a different canvas or workspace. The rule "a pane turned to a page still on its way keeps what it drew" stays for a page turn inside one canvas. Check the platform side by reading only: it keeps one CanvasView per PaneId and removes it when no scene names the pane (platform/mod.rs:414-434), so equal ids in two workspaces must not show the old picture.
5. Focus is per workspace and by id. Shared::follow: for the same workspace, focus stays on the same id, or, when that pane is gone, goes to the pane now at its old number (today's rule); for another workspace, to the pane that had focus there earlier in this run, else the first.
6. Go through the other state keyed by PaneId and make a switch safe for each: Canvases.pen, handle, steps and turning; Shared.menu (close it); the web views' key (platform/web.rs:178-182, by pane and item).
7. canvases/kept.rs:48,64 keeps PaneId::number on disk for a pane waiting for a page (slinger-857848). It now holds the server's id, which is stable. Update the comments at layout/tree.rs:33-38 and ARCHITECTURE.md near line 1249. A file written by an older build may name a pane by position: the worst case is a pane that does not turn.

Tests (pure: canvases/tests.rs or canvases/view tests, shared/tests.rs, panes tests, layout/tree/tests.rs): close A in "row A B": B keeps its viewport, page and trail. Workspace A, then B, then A, with equal pane ids in both: B's pane starts with a new view; back in A the viewport, page and trail are as left. Before B's page comes, show() returns no draw that came from A. A pane opened by someone else (a new layout through follow) moves no other view. Focus per workspace. The id-0 fallback.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md app rows (panes.rs, canvases, layout/tree). CHANGELOG, Fixed: a workspace no longer opens at another workspace's zoom and scroll or shows its ink; closing a pane no longer moves the other panes' views.

title: app: a first open fits the content; a zoom-to-fit command
description:
Owner decision: a first open fits the content. Today every view starts at Viewport::start(): origin 16 points in, 100% (crates/app/src/layout.rs:104-107), whatever the page holds, and the zoom commands are in, out and 100% only (canvases/paging.rs:47-54).

Add:
1. Viewport::fitting(content: Rect, size: Size) in crates/app/src/layout.rs, pure: zoom = the smaller of 100% and the zoom at which the content with CANVAS_MARGIN on each side fits the screen on both axes, held at MIN_ZOOM; the content's top-left corner sits CANVAS_MARGIN screen points in from the pane's top left (as Viewport::at). It never zooms above 100%. Content of no size, or a size or content that is not finite, gives Viewport::start(). layout.rs has a 100% coverage floor.
2. A pure function for a page's extent in crates/app/src/scene/canvas.rs: the union of the bounds of the items as the pane shows them (the bounds code is already there, near line 334); None for an empty page. Inside a box the extent is the room.
3. A view that has no place yet (new in a workspace, or started again by step 5's canvas change) is "unplaced". Canvases::show places it with fitting() the first time its page has come, once. Later changes to the page do not move it. A pan or zoom on an unplaced view places it at start() first. Reader mode (canvases/reader.rs) is untouched: a PDF pane fits its column as it does now.
4. Command::ZoomToFit, name "zoom-to-fit", label "Zoom to fit", default key cmd+9 (cmd+1 and cmd+8 are taken in crates/app/src/commands.rs; check the keymap test for a clash). It goes in Command::ALL, so the palette, the key overlay and the View menu beside zoom-reset (commands/menu.rs:159) get it. In canvases/paging.rs it fits the focused pane's page (the room inside a box) and flashes the zoom as the other zoom commands do; on a reader pane it does nothing, as they do; on a pane with no canvas it flashes NO_CANVAS. Add it wherever zoom-reset is listed (panes.rs:225, commands/registry.rs:77,173, config.example.toml and the key docs: grep "zoom-reset").

Tests: layout tests for fitting (small content stays at 100% with the margin; wide and tall content zoom out to fit; the MIN_ZOOM hold; each degenerate input). canvases tests: the first show of a page whose items are far from the origin has them in view; a second show after a pan does not refit; an empty page is start(); zoom-to-fit after a pan away brings the content back; inside a box it fits the room; a reader pane is unchanged. commands tests: the name, the key, the palette row.

description:
Owner decision: a split copies the source pane's view. Today the new pane gets View::default(): the first page at the start view (crates/app/src/canvases.rs:440-444); only the pane's content is copied (panes.rs:124-130, shared.rs:233-236).

Add one function on Canvases (in canvases/view.rs) that copies a view from one PaneId to another, and call it where the command runs with both Shared and Canvases in hand (crates/app/src/route.rs run, or window.rs). The copy counts as placed: the fit of the step before does not run on it. After the split the two views are independent.

'Step in beside' (crates/app/src/window/items.rs:107-115) splits and then steps the new pane in: its step-out view (Trail's back, canvases/step.rs:186-188) is now the source pane's view, which falls out of the copy. title: core, control, daemon: the daemon keeps per-pane views and focus; a pane_view verb
description:
Owner decisions: view state (page, pan, zoom, and the focused pane) lives in the daemon; pane splits stay with the workspace file. Follow "Adding a verb" in docs/service.md: core, then crates/control, then the daemon's answer, then clients.

Core, new crates/core/src/workspace/view.rs (owns the format and the rules; no IO):
- PaneView { canvas, page: Option<String>, x, y, zoom }: the canvas and page the pane looked at, the canvas point at the pane's top left, and the zoom.
- Views { focus: Option<pane id>, panes: map from pane id to PaneView } for one workspace.
- Rules: set(id, view) refuses a number that is not finite or a zoom of 0 or less (Error::Invalid with a hint); keep(ids) drops the views of panes not in the layout and a focus that names none; copy(from, to); view_of(id, target) gives a view only when its canvas is what the pane shows now. Text form: JSON with a version; text that cannot be read is no views, never an error.

Daemon, new crates/daemon/src/views.rs (workspaces.rs is 493 lines): one file, workspaces/views.json in the data directory, {"v":1,"workspaces":{"<directory of the workspace's file>":<Views>}}, keyed by the directory because that is how the daemon knows an open workspace (workspaces/open.json). Written whole and synced when it changes, one change at a time. Never in slinger-workspace.toml and never in a canvas file. A missing or unreadable file is no views. A view change appends no event to the record: the log is append-only and views change often. Closing a workspace keeps its views, so opening it again restores them.

Control (crates/control/src/pane.rs, 241 lines): PaneAsk::PaneView { workspace, views: [{id, canvas, page?, x, y, zoom}], focus? }, written by the same small type as the other pane verbs (the app builds no Request: docs/service.md step 2). Pane gets an optional "view"; PaneLayout gets an optional "focus" (a pane id). Client::pane_view. All additions are optional fields, so the protocol version stays 1.

Daemon answer (crates/daemon/src/server/pane.rs): every pane reply carries each pane's stored view (when its canvas is the pane's target) and the focus. pane_view stores the views and focus it names and replies as pane_list does; an id that is not in the layout is ignored and the verb still succeeds. pane_open beside a pane copies that pane's stored view to the new id when both show the same target. pane_close and any change prune views to the layout's ids.

Clients: the app sends pane_view in the next step. The CLI gets no new command (an agent has no use for setting the user's view); 'slinger pane list --json' shows view and focus through serde, which lets an agent see where the user looks.

Tests: core view tests (each rule; round trip; unreadable text). control wire-line tests for the new ask and for replies with and without view and focus. daemon tests/pane.rs through a real socket: set then list returns the view and focus; they survive a daemon restart on the same data directory; pane_close prunes; pane_open beside copies; an unknown id is ignored; a zoom of 0 is "invalid"; two workspaces do not share views; pane_view leaves the bytes of slinger-workspace.toml unchanged and appends no event.

Docs, same commit: docs/service.md (the verb table, "Panes", and "Data directory": workspaces/views.json); ARCHITECTURE.md (core workspace/view.rs, daemon views.rs, server/pane.rs row near line 283, control); SPEC.md section 5 line 63 ("It holds no durable state"): the server keeps the arrangement and the views, the app keeps only its window chrome (frame, sidebar, last workspace) in the user defaults; docs/cli.md pane list JSON; CHANGELOG.

title: app: restore each pane's view and the focus from the daemon; save them as they change
description:
Owner decision: reopening restores the last view. This step makes the app read the views the daemon keeps (the step before) and send its own.

Read:
- The Watch's layout news carries the stored views and focus (they are in the pane_list reply). The Watch decides "the layout changed" on the arrangement only (workspace, tree, ids, targets, ratios) and ignores view and focus, so the app's own saves do not come back as layout news and do not fetch the UI code again (backend.rs:118-121 fetches it for every fresh layout).
- When a pane of (workspace, id) has no view in memory (first sight in this run, or a pane someone else opened), it takes the stored view if that view's canvas is the pane's: page, origin and zoom, the zoom held in MIN_ZOOM..=MAX_ZOOM by a Viewport constructor in layout.rs (100% coverage floor). Such a view is placed: the first-open fit does not run. With no stored view the pane is unplaced and fits its content. A view in memory always wins over a stored one.
- The first time a workspace is shown in this run, focus goes to the stored focus, if that pane is there.
- A PDF pane needs nothing more: the reader refits its column on each draw and keeps the top (Viewport::reading), so the stored origin restores the scroll.
- The box trail is not stored: a relaunch opens outside the box.

Write:
- A pure function gives the current workspace's looks: for each canvas pane its id, canvas, the page it shows (the page's id once it has come) and viewport, and the focused pane's id. main.rs compares it with the last one handed over after an event that drew, and hands a changed one to a new worker, crates/app/src/backend/views.rs (shaped like Outbox: the main thread never waits). The worker waits until 300 ms pass with no newer looks, then sends one pane_view with the panes that changed. A failed send is tried again with the next looks and is otherwise dropped: a lost view is not worth a problem on screen. Build the worker over a send function so a unit test can count requests.
- A switch to another workspace sends the old workspace's looks without the wait.
- Quit: the red close button ends the app without the answer hearing of it (crates/app/src/platform/mod.rs:275-280), and Step::Quit goes the same way (mod.rs:320). Add Event::Quitting, dispatched in close_and_quit before terminate (platform only translates; if the window-lifecycle work has added a quit event by then, use that one). The answer hands over the looks and waits for the worker at most 500 ms: the client's own timeout is 30 s (crates/control/src/client.rs:25), so wait on the thread, not on the call.

Mind the caps: main.rs 473 lines, canvases.rs after step 5, platform/mod.rs after step 2.

Tests: with the real daemon helper: pan, zoom and turn the page, flush, and pane_list has the view; a new Canvases that follows that layout shows the pane on the stored page at the stored viewport, with no fit; a stored view for another canvas is ignored; a view in memory wins over a later layout's stored view; a pane_view sent from elsewhere gives no layout news from the Watch; focus is restored. Worker unit tests: many looks inside the wait make one request with only the changed panes; the flush at quit sends at once and returns within its bound when the daemon does not answer.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (backend/views.rs, the Watch's news, Event::Quitting, canvases/view.rs); CHANGELOG, Added: a pane opens on the page, pan and zoom you left it at, on this machine, after a switch, a relaunch or a daemon restart.

title: app: close a workspace from its sidebar row: a close mark per row, close by folder
description:
Goal: every workspace row in the sidebar has a ✕ that closes that workspace without showing it first; close-workspace (opt+cmd+W, File menu, palette, a broken row's 'Close workspace' line) still closes the shown one. Key unchanged.

Files. crates/app/src/scene/sidebar.rs is 470 lines: first move the layout (`laid`, `Line`, `block`) into a new scene/sidebar/rows.rs, a pure move. scene/taps.rs: add `Tap::Close(usize)` (the sidebar's workspace with this index; resolved to its folder at the tap, as Tap::Workspace is). Sidebar: replace `close()` with `dir(index) -> Option<PathBuf>` (a lookup; `shown_dir` stays) and `closed(&mut self, dir: &Path) -> bool`, which takes that row out and returns whether it was the shown one (then `shown = None`, so `at()` picks as it does today). In the layout, each workspace's name line gets a ✕ in theme.muted at the sidebar's right edge with a target style::TAP (28 pt) wide and the row high; the name's label ends before it; these targets come before the row targets in the list, because Taps finds the first frame that holds the point, and the merge of a workspace's lines into one row target must still work. A collapsed sidebar has none. window.rs: `close_workspace` takes the folder, asks the daemon first (backend::close_workspace), on Ok calls `sidebar.closed` and flashes 'Closed <name>' (the folder's name for a nameless broken file), on Err flashes the problem and leaves the row; it returns whether the shown one closed. `tap()` gets a `Tap::Close(_) => {}` arm. route.rs: the arm for `Ask::Run(Command::CloseWorkspace)` passes `sidebar.shown_dir()`, a new `Ask::Tap((_, Tap::Close(i)))` case passes `sidebar.dir(i)`; answer `Routed::Watch(None, ..)` only when the shown workspace closed, else `Routed::Answer(Step::Draw(..))`. window.rs is 495 lines: keep it net-zero (the lit-target code in `view` already lights a sidebar target; check the ✕ lights alone).

title: app: one pure enabled predicate; menu bar items grey out when their command cannot act
description:
Goal: one pure function says whether a command can act now, and the menu bar greys the items it says no to. Later steps reuse it for context menus.

Files. New crates/app/src/commands/able.rs (pure, no scene types): `pub struct Facts` and `pub fn can(command: Command, facts: &Facts) -> bool` as one exhaustive match with no `_` arm, so a new command must decide. Facts holds only what the rules read, for example: how many panes; whether the focused pane shows a canvas or an agent UI; how many items are selected there and whether one is a box; whether a box can be stepped into (canvases.step_target) and whether the pane is stepped in; how many pages; whether a find is active; whether a workspace shows and whether its agent exists and runs; whether a notice shows. commands/menu.rs: `Item` gains `pub enabled: bool`; `bar(keys, checked, facts)` sets it from `can` (a native item stays true: the window validates cut, copy and paste through Event::Can as today); add `pub fn same_layout(a: &[Menu], b: &[Menu]) -> bool`, true when two bars differ only in `enabled`. New crates/app/src/window/facts.rs: `pub fn facts(shared, canvases, sidebar, area) -> Facts` from existing queries; a missing read-only accessor goes in the canvases/ file that owns that state (canvases.rs is 497 lines: add nothing there). window.rs `view` passes the facts to `bar`; window.rs is 495 lines, so move a self-contained part out if needed (for example `finder` and `export_ui` to window/files.rs). platform/menu.rs: `Target` answers `validateMenuItem:` with the `enabled` of the item with that tag in the newest model (the MADE thread-local); `show` keeps the NSMenu and only stores the new model when `same_layout` holds, and rebuilds otherwise as now.

The rule for `can`: false only where `window::run` for that command would now do nothing or only flash a refusal; when unsure, true. Read each command's code before deciding. Starting list to verify: ClosePane, GrowPane, ShrinkPane and the Focus commands need more than one pane; ExportUi needs an agent UI pane; DeleteSelection, Duplicate and the Nudges need a selection; ClearSelection needs a selection or a stepped-in pane (it steps out); Fold needs a selected box; StepIn and StepInBeside need a step target; StepOut needs a stepped-in pane; NextPage, PreviousPage and RemovePage need a second page; FindNext needs a find; CloseWorkspace and ShowWorkspaceFolder need a shown workspace; StartAgent needs an agent that does not run, StopAgent one that runs, RestartAgent an agent; DismissNotice needs a notice. Undo and Redo stay on (the app does not know the daemon's undo stack). Sling stays on for a canvas pane (with nothing selected it slings what is new).

Keys do not change: AppKit does not fire a disabled item for its key, so the key reaches the keymap and the command answers as before. Say so in the module doc of commands/menu.rs and in ARCHITECTURE.md's Keys section.

Tests. commands/able tests: one case per rule, both ways. commands/menu/tests.rs: `bar` greys what `can` refuses; natives stay enabled; `same_layout` is true for an enabled-only change and false for a title, key, check or order change; the existing tests still pass with a Facts in which everything can act. crates/app/src/tests/able.rs with the World and a real daemon: for several states (nothing selected, one pane, one page, a canvas pane) every command `can` refuses is run through route() and changes nothing (item count, pane count, page count); and a command it allows (delete with a selection) acts. A key for a refused command still answers as before.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (commands.rs, window.rs, platform/menu.rs), CHANGELOG.md. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle, open each menu with and without a selection, on an agent UI pane, with one pane and one page: the right items are grey and none is grey that would work; a greyed item's key still flashes why; Cut, Copy and Paste still grey as before; an item's state is right the moment the menu opens.

title: app: the standard Mac menus: Hide, Hide Others, Show All, Services, Full Screen, Zoom, Window, Help
description:

title: app: right and middle button events reach the app; a pure module tells a context click from a pan
description:
Goal: the decision 'click or drag' for the right button moves out of platform into a tested pure module. A right drag and a middle drag pan as before. A right click (and a ctrl+click, a two-finger trackpad click, a tablet button set to right click) no longer pans by its jitter; it focuses the pane under it. Step 5 makes it open a menu.

Files. platform/mod.rs is 498 lines: first move `Event` and `Step` into a new platform/event.rs and re-export them (a pure move; main.rs keeps importing them from crate::platform). New pure crates/app/src/scene/secondary.rs: `Button {Secondary, Middle}`, `Phase {Down, Drag, Up}` and a `Secondary` state with `down(button, at)`, `drag(at) -> Option<(Point, f64, f64)>` (the press point and the delta to pan by; None until the pointer is more than SLOP, 4 pt, from the press, then the whole way so far, so the canvas does not lag the pointer) and `up(at) -> Option<Point>` (the press point when a Secondary press never passed the slop: a context click; never for Middle; None with no press). Model it on scene/hand.rs. Keep it in Shared beside `hand`. platform/event.rs: `Event::Button { button, phase, at }`. platform/input.rs: RightMouseDown/Dragged/Up and OtherMouse* with button 2 dispatch Event::Button and return what dispatch returns; the RIGHT cell goes. A LeftMouseDown with control held is sent as Secondary Down, and the LeftMouseDragged and LeftMouseUp after it as Secondary Drag and Up (one Cell<bool> is the only state): macOS defines ctrl+click as the secondary click. Update the module docs of input.rs and platform/mod.rs. route.rs: handle Event::Button before `asked`, as `hand` is: Down is taken (Step::Stay) except over an open entry field (canvases.sling_covers(at), and the feedback and rename entries if they have a field there), where it is Step::Pass so the native text menu shows; Drag pans through window::gesture with Event::Scroll { at: press point, dx, dy } exactly as the platform's scroll did (over a pane that is not a canvas it passes, as today); Up with a click moves the pointer (tools.moved), focuses the pane under it as a press does (Shared::press_focus) and draws; under the key overlay, the palette, the page menu or an open tool pop-up it does nothing.

Consequence to state in the CHANGELOG: because the app takes the right press, WebKit's own menu (Reload, Back) no longer opens over an agent UI pane or a live item.

Tests. scene/secondary/tests.rs: a lift inside the slop is a click at the press point; a drag past the slop pans by the whole movement and the lift is then no click; coming back inside the slop after leaving it is still a pan; the middle button pans and never clicks; an up or a drag with no down is nothing; a second down replaces the first. crates/app/src/tests/secondary.rs with the World and a real daemon: a Secondary down, drags and up move the viewport as the same Event::Scroll deltas do; a click leaves the viewport and the canvas unchanged and focuses the pane under it; a Down over the open sling entry passes; a middle drag pans.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (platform/ paragraph, route and shared), docs/design/pen-less.md (the right button: drag pans, click is the context click; a tablet button set to right click does the same), CHANGELOG.md. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle and on real hardware, right drag and middle drag pan as before with a mouse; a two-finger trackpad click and a ctrl+click pan nothing; ctrl+drag pans; a Wacom side switch set to right click acts as a right button; the sling entry's field still shows the system text menu on a right click; an agent UI no longer shows WebKit's menu.

title: app: a context click pops a native menu for a pane, a footer or the empty canvas
description:
Goal: the first whole slice: a context click (step 4) on the empty part of a canvas, on a pane's footer or on an agent UI pane opens an NSMenu whose items come from a pure function; a pick runs the command on the pane the click focused.

Files. New pure crates/app/src/commands/context.rs: `pub enum Subject { Canvas { stepped: bool }, Pane { ui: bool } }` (later steps add variants), `pub struct Popup { pub at: Point, pub items: Vec<Item> }` and `pub fn items(subject: &Subject, keys: &Keymap, checked: Command, facts: &Facts) -> Vec<Item>`. It builds each Item as `bar` does (share that one constructor in commands/menu.rs): title from Command::title, key from the live keymap (not one that types), `enabled` from able::can, separators as Action::Separator. Menus: Canvas = Paste (native), New text, Select all, separator, Sling now, separator, Zoom to 100%, Dotted grid, separator, New page, Step out of box. Pane = Export agent UI… (only when `ui`), separator, Split right, Split down, Close pane. platform/event.rs: `Step::Menu(Popup, Box<Scene>)`. platform/mod.rs `dispatch`: draw the scene, then pop the menu, after the borrow of the answer is dropped (a pick dispatches a new event from inside the pop); `reply` treats it as a draw. platform/menu.rs: `pop(popup, view, mtm)` builds an NSMenu from the items with the existing `made()`, sets autoenablesItems off and each item's enabled from its Item (a native item in a popup is always enabled: a paste that goes nowhere flashes why, as its key does), and calls popUpMenuPositioningItem:atLocation:inView: at the point flipped to the view. Its command items go to the existing `run:`, so a pick arrives as Event::Command and acts on what the click made current. The timer fires while the menu is open (chrome::tick_after uses the common modes): the menu bar must not be rebuilt under it for an enabled-only change (step 2's same_layout). New crates/app/src/window/context.rs (window.rs is 495 lines): `subject_at(at, shared, canvases, area) -> Option<Subject>` from Panes::place and status::content: a footer or an agent UI pane is Pane, a canvas pane's content is Canvas { stepped } (later steps look for an item, a divider and the sidebar first). route.rs: the context click of step 4 now answers Step::Menu(Popup { at, items }, view) when there is a subject; tools.moved(at) has run, so 'New text' lands at the click.

Tests. commands/context tests: each subject's items in order; a rebound key shows on its item and a key that types does not; `enabled` follows `can` (Close pane is grey with one pane, Step out of box unless stepped in); no menu starts or ends with a separator or has two in a row; no command twice; 'Export agent UI…' only for an agent UI pane. crates/app/src/tests/context.rs with the World and a real daemon: a context click on the empty canvas answers Step::Menu with the Canvas items at that point; on a footer, and on an agent UI pane, the Pane items, and that pane has focus; under the open palette nothing; after the click Event::Command(Command::NewText) starts a text at the clicked point; Event::Command(Command::SplitRight) splits the clicked pane.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (commands.rs, window.rs, platform/menu.rs, the Step list in platform/), CHANGELOG.md. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle, a right click, a ctrl+click and a two-finger click open the menu at the pointer on release, also on a second display and in full screen; a right drag still pans and opens nothing; each item runs; Escape and a click outside close it; an agent's change arriving while the menu is open does not close or break it.

title: app: context menus for canvas items by kind, the selection and a text being typed
description:
Goal: a context click on a canvas item opens a menu for that kind of item; on a selection, one for the selection. Finder's rule: a click on an item outside the selection selects it alone first; a click on a selected item, or inside the selection's box where a press would grab it, keeps the selection. The commands then act on the selection as they always do.

Files. New crates/app/src/canvases/context.rs (canvases.rs is 497 lines) with `impl Canvases`: `item_at(&self, panes, (pane, frame), at) -> Option<Hit>` where Hit says the item's kind (text, box and whether folded, arrow, stroke, pdf, live), and whether it is in the selection; and `select_only(&mut self, panes, pane, id)`. Reuse the select tool's own hit test (`topmost` in scene/select/pick.rs with REACH / zoom; make it pub(crate) rather than copy it) and canvases/live.rs `under` for a live item; honour the stepped-in view and folded boxes as a press does. Check in the code whether a live item and a pdf item can be selected, and leave out of their menus what cannot act. commands/context.rs: add `Subject::Item { kind }`, `Subject::Selection { count, has_box }` and `Subject::Typing` and their menus. Any item: Sling selection, separator, Cut, Copy (natives), Duplicate, Delete selection, separator, Pick a colour. A text adds Pick a text size, Bigger text, Smaller text. A box adds Fold or unfold box, Step into box, Step into box beside. A pdf adds Crop PDF and Show canvas file in Finder. A live item: Sling selection, Delete selection. Selection (more than one): Sling selection, separator, Cut, Copy, Duplicate, Delete selection, separator, Fold or unfold box (when it has a box), Pick a colour, Select nothing. Typing (a canvas text is being typed under the click): Cut, Copy, Paste only, and the text does not end. window/context.rs: `subject_at` looks for an item in a canvas pane before it answers Canvas, and the route selects per the rule before it builds the popup (the Facts must be read after the selection changed). Pick a colour and Pick a text size open their pop-up at the pointer, which the click already moved.

Tests. commands/context tests: each kind's items in order, the separator rules, Fold only with a box. canvases/context tests or crates/app/src/tests/context_items.rs with the World and a real daemon holding a text, an open box, a folded box and an arrow: a context click on the box selects it alone and answers the box menu; on one of two selected items it keeps both and answers the Selection menu; on an item while another is selected it selects the clicked one; then Event::Command(Command::DeleteSelection) deletes exactly the selection and Event::Command(Command::Fold) folds the clicked box; in a pane stepped into a box the click hits what the pane shows; a click on a text being typed answers the Typing menu and the text is still being typed.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (canvases/context.rs, commands.rs), CHANGELOG.md. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle, right-click a stroke, a text, an open and a folded box, an arrow, a pdf page, a live item and a multi-selection: the clicked item is selected and each item does what it says; Cut, Copy and Paste from the menu work on items and inside a text being typed.

title: app: context menus for sidebar workspace rows and pane dividers; a pick carries its subject
description:
Goal: a context click on a workspace's rows in the sidebar offers Close workspace, Show workspace folder in Finder, Start agent, Stop agent and Restart agent for that workspace, whichever one the window shows, with no switch. A context click on a divider offers Grow pane and Shrink pane for that divider. A context click on the rest of the sidebar offers Open workspace… and Show or hide sidebar. These are the subjects that cannot be made current, so the pick carries its subject.

Files. commands/context.rs: add `Subject::Workspace { dir: PathBuf, .. }` (the folder names it, as workspace_close takes; never the row's index), `Subject::Divider { before: u32, ratio: f64 }` (the number of the pane before it, as pane_resize names it, and its split's share now) and `Subject::Sidebar`; `Popup` gains `pub subject: Subject`. Menus: Workspace = Close workspace, Show workspace folder in Finder, separator, Start agent, Stop agent, Restart agent in a new conversation; Divider = Grow pane, Shrink pane; Sidebar = Open workspace…, Show or hide sidebar. The Facts for a Workspace menu describe that row's workspace and agent, not the shown one's, so Start and Stop grey for it. platform/event.rs: `Event::Picked(Command, Subject)`. platform/menu.rs: a popup's command items get their own action (`pick:`), which dispatches Event::Picked with the popup's subject; the menu bar's `run:` is unchanged and still sends Event::Command. The app keeps no memory of the last popup. main.rs `ask` (473 lines; put new arms in window/context.rs if it would pass 500): Event::Picked closes what is open as Event::Command does, then asks `Ask::On(command, subject)`. route.rs and main's `asked`: for Subject::Workspace, CloseWorkspace goes to step 1's window::close_workspace with that folder; StartAgent, StopAgent and RestartAgent to window::agent, which now takes the folder (the key and the menu bar pass sidebar.shown_dir()); ShowWorkspaceFolder reveals that folder (window::finder takes it). For Subject::Divider, GrowPane and ShrinkPane move that divider by panes::STEP, held in the ratio's limits, locally (Panes::set_ratio) and at the daemon (Shared::resized), as a drag of it does. Any other subject or command runs as Ask::Run(command). window/context.rs `subject_at` order: the sidebar (a row is a Workspace; add `Sidebar::row_at(at, ..) -> Option<usize>` from the same layout its targets come from; elsewhere Sidebar), then a divider (Panes::divider_at), then a pane's item, canvas or footer. A click on step 1's ✕ target opens the row's menu too.

Tests. commands/context tests: the three menus; Start agent grey for a row whose agent runs and Stop grey for one that does not, whatever the shown workspace is. crates/app/src/tests/context_rows.rs with the World, the sidebar open and a real daemon with two workspaces: a context click on the row that is not shown answers Step::Menu with Subject::Workspace of its folder and does not change the shown workspace; Event::Picked(CloseWorkspace, that subject) closes that workspace in the daemon, answers Routed::Answer and leaves the shown one; Event::Picked(ShowWorkspaceFolder, ..) resolves that folder (test the pure part, window::finder); a context click with no pick followed by Event::Command(Command::CloseWorkspace) closes the shown workspace, not the clicked one; a context click on a divider answers Subject::Divider and Event::Picked(GrowPane, ..) moves that divider's share by one step and no other divider.

Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md (the command path: Event::Command against Event::Picked; window.rs, platform/menu.rs), CHANGELOG.md. docs/hand-check.md, one line: in the bundle, right-click a workspace that is not shown: Close closes it and the window does not switch; Start, Stop and Restart act on that row's agent and the flash names it; Show folder opens its folder; right-click a divider and grow and shrink it; right-click the empty sidebar and open a workspace.

Pass: type, move and edit a multi-paragraph markdown text with real vim keys in a driven window; buffer lands in the canvas item; key-to-paint latency measured; the scene editor stays as the fallback. Column is 80 cells (the owner's textwidth). Report findings, do not ship.

title: figures: an agent draws with code (script API, figure and parts, fill/dash/lock)
description: Design draft and engine spike result: docs/design/figures.md (owner to confirm; six questions under 'For the owner'). Reference: the tutor's tldraw worksheet. Pick: QuickJS in a new crates/script; a figure is its script and its data; canvas draw / redraw / figure. Next step after the owner confirms: sd plan from the doc's build order (8 steps).

title: design: close the gaps in docs/design/figures.md before code
description:
Finish docs/design/figures.md so every later step reads one settled contract. Design each open point twice (B6) and record the pick.
- Canvas file: how fill, dash, heads, closed, locked, fig, part are written (optional fields on known kinds; old-reader rule as docs/design/fold.md). A headless line: arrow with heads none, or a two-point stroke. Which module holds the new style values: canvas/item.rs is 457 lines and file/json.rs 447 (limit 500), so name the new module(s).
- Draw order: fills under all ink and text, above PDF pages, in the core raster and in the app (paper_first in scene/ink/shown.rs; a folded box's peek panel must stay on top).
- Lock: a table of every gesture and whether it skips a locked item (eraser, lasso, tap, marquee, select-all, text tool, arrow binding, fold mark, crop). The unlock/lock UX and command names. Paste and duplicate drop fig, part and locked.
- Part address grammar (figure/part), figure name rules, what a name clash does.
- figure_drawn payload and where the script lives (a blob, as ui put). Replace-by-match algorithm for a redraw. How crates/script hands shapes to the daemon without linking the core.
- Colour: a fill's rule in the dark theme (legible() must not flip it).
- Amend SPEC D6 and section 4 in the same commit. Add the six "For the owner" picks to docs/open-picks.md under a "Figures" heading (they are picks, not blockers).
Done when: the doc has no "not designed yet", and check:debt and check:agents pass.
Owner decisions of 2026-11-24 are in docs/design/figures.md "Decided by the owner": they are settled, so they do NOT go in docs/open-picks.md (only picks made after that do). Design the grab-a-figure-as-one unlock (no stored toggle, no single-item unlock: the gesture table and the command follow from it) and the colour grammar: defaults that nest (figure, part, group), and the open point of named theme colours beside hex.
Named theme colours beside hex are decided (owner, 2026-11-24): pick the exact names and the plot series, and design twice whether a name is stored on the item (theme-aware later) or resolved to hex at run time.

title: core: items take fill, dash, heads and closed; file, ops and raster
description:
Per docs/design/figures.md "The model". Add the four optional fields to the item model, the canvas file (read, write, set/laid_over in file/json.rs), canvas apply ops and canvas show output. Render them in render/raster.rs: fill (box, closed stroke) drawn under all ink and text and above a PDF page; dashed and dotted lines; arrow heads end/both/none; a closed stroke joins its ends.
Watch: item.rs 457, json.rs 447, file/mod.rs 472, log.rs 484 lines (limit 500): put the style in its own module. crates/core/tests/render.rs holds golden images; existing goldens must not change (a canvas with none of the new fields renders byte-identical). Add a test that a file with the new fields survives a reader that does not know them (the fold.md old-reader test is the pattern). Update docs/design/canvas-file.md, docs/service.md and docs/cli.md (canvas schema) in the same commit.
Named colours are in (see docs/design/figures.md "Colour"): if the design stores names on items, the colour field and the raster take them here.

title: app: draw fill, dash, dotted, arrow heads and closed strokes
description:
Read the new fields in mirror.rs::read (:353) and mirror/write.rs; carry them on scene Shape/Mark (scene/canvas.rs :34, :84, barbs :461) and paint them in platform/canvas.rs::paint (:180). Mark::Panel already has fill and one dash constant (DASH, :55): reuse it and add a dotted pattern. Fills need their own pass: after PDF pages (paper_first, scene/ink/shown.rs:104), before all ink; a folded box's peek panel (canvases/fold.rs::drawn) stays above. A fill colour is not passed through legible() (scene/canvas.rs:447); use the rule the design picked. closed needs smooth::smooth to close the curve.
Watch sizes: scene/canvas.rs 472, platform/canvas.rs 454, mirror.rs 458, scene.rs 496: split first (e.g. scene/canvas/arrow.rs, a fill pass module). drive/outline.rs::mark (:97) prints filled/dashed/dotted/heads so an agent can self-check; tests in tests/drive.rs and scene/canvas/tests.rs pin the format.
Self-check on a scratch daemon with slinger-app --drive and read the scene and the PNG.
Decided: the agent colour is a theme config key (config/theme.rs); fills are always under ink, nothing raises one.
Named colours are in: if the design stores names on items, the theme maps them here (config/theme.rs) and in the core raster.

title: core: items take locked, fig and part; a part address names an item
description: Per docs/design/figures.md "Figure and part". Optional fields locked, fig, part on any item; canvas file, apply ops and show output as the previous step. A part address (figure/part) resolves wherever an item id is taken: start at Log::named (file/put.rs:275) so put --beside, edit, remove, crop and read --in all get it from one place. A part of several items resolves to their joint frame for placement. Canvas lists its figures (name, frame, parts). locked is for the user's hands only: the author rule (Canvas::may_change, canvas/mod.rs:285) is unchanged and an agent still edits its own locked items. An op to lock and unlock items, usable by the user and by the maker. Old-reader test as before. Docs in the same commit.

title: app: the pen skips locked items; unlock figure grabs it as one
description:
There is no single choke point. Skip locked items in: takes() (scene/select.rs:426: select, lasso, select-all), the eraser (Select::drag :164), innermost (select/pick.rs:118), text_at (scene/shapes.rs:440), bind::target (scene/shapes/bind.rs:14), mark_under (canvases/fold.rs:100), crop topmost (scene/crop.rs:57). Follow the gesture table in docs/design/figures.md. Writing ink over a locked item must work as on empty paper.
Add the lock/unlock commands the design named: Command enum + ALL + chord + registry title/group + menu row (commands.rs, commands/registry.rs, commands/menu.rs); commands/tests.rs pins order, chords and titles; docs/app-parity.md lists them. Paste and duplicate drop fig, part and locked (mirror/clip.rs::pasted keeps unknown keys today). The drive outline prints locked. commands.rs is 454 lines, scene/select.rs 439.
Self-check with slinger drive: erase and lasso across a locked figure, then unlock and move it. What only a hand can judge goes in docs/hand-check.md.
Decided: one command, "unlock figure", on the figure under the pointer: it selects the whole figure as one unit (move, duplicate, delete) and the figure is locked again when deselected. No lock/unlock toggle and no single-item unlock. A duplicate of a whole figure is a new figure with a new name (design step says how).

title: core: the packet names figures and parts; read --in takes a part
description: Per docs/design/figures.md "In the packet". A figure is one line (name, frame, its parts), not one line per item; the user's new ink over a part carries over=figure/part; canvas read --in figure/part gives that part's contents and the ink over it. Files: packet/build.rs, line.rs, format.rs, areas.rs, canvas/file/packet.rs. Packet v1 allows added fields; stored packet snapshots in crates/core/tests must still read. Decide and test what a folded box holding a figure prints. Update docs/design/packet.md.

title: crates/script: run a drawing script in QuickJS, bounded and pure
description:
New crate crates/script (slinger-script), linked only by the daemon. One function: (script, data, read-only view) -> shapes + warnings, or an error with line:col. Engine rquickjs (quickjs-ng, MIT); the API is a JS prelude over one native emit call, as the spike (see docs/design/figures.md "The script API" and Appendix A; the spike itself is gone, rebuild from the doc). Limits: 1 s (interrupt handler), 32 MB, 512 KB stack, 1 MiB script, 5,000 items; no Date, timers, console, imports, IO. Deterministic: same inputs, same bytes out.
From the fluency test: arrow takes line's arguments or (from, to); bad arguments fail at the call by name; arrow labels sit beside the arrow, not on it; warn on text over a line and on overlap.
Gates: layer rules in budgets/layer-rules.json in the same commit (only-daemon-runs-scripts: forbid slinger_script outside crates/daemon and crates/script; script-is-pure: as core-is-pure plus std::fs). unsafe_code is denied workspace-wide: no unsafe in the wrapper. deny.toml: licenses and crates.io-only sources must pass with the -sys crate in Cargo.lock; pick the feature set with pre-generated bindings (no libclang). check:deps (machete) and the 86% coverage floor apply. The app and CLI dev-depend on slingerd, so their test builds compile QuickJS: note the build-time cost.
Build for all four release targets (aarch64/x86_64 apple-darwin, aarch64/x86_64 linux-gnu): cross-check x86_64-apple-darwin locally; for Linux say plainly what was and was not built. Tests: the worksheet script (Appendix B) gives 56 items and 15 parts; infinite loop, memory bomb and deep recursion each stop with a clear error. ARCHITECTURE.md gains the crate and the boundary.
Decided: QuickJS in process; whole units; default colour is the agent colour passed in by the daemon; colour defaults nest (fig.color, part, group, stack, table, plot) and the nearest wins. Named theme colours only if the design step picked them.
Named colours are in: the API takes the names the design step picked wherever it takes hex; an unknown name fails at the call and lists the names.

title: core: place a set of shapes as a figure, and replace it in place
description: The core half of canvas draw (docs/design/figures.md "The verbs"). Input: a name, shapes in figure coordinates with parts, a placement (beside an id, over an id, at a point, in a box), the author. Output: one undo step that adds the items with fig/part set. Placement reuses free_beside; --over lays the frame on the target without moving anything. A draw to a name that exists replaces by match (part + order): unchanged items are not rewritten, so the same input twice writes nothing; the user's ink is never touched; only the maker may redraw. Record event figure_drawn {canvas, figure, script, data, origin} in record/body.rs (payload, kind, from_parts; not in KINDS, as ui_put); crates/core/tests/record.rs pins the format. A render entry for shapes not yet on a canvas (render::draw at render/mod.rs:162 is private) for --dry-run. The reply also counts as reply_landed (sling::landed, sling.rs:240).

title: control, daemon, CLI: canvas draw, with --dry-run --png
description:
Follow "Adding a verb" in docs/service.md. slinger canvas draw <CANVAS> <FILE> --name N (--beside ID | --over ID | --at X,Y | --in ID) [--data JSON|@FILE] [--dry-run] [--png PATH]. The script crosses the socket as a file path, as ui put (daemon/src/server.rs:357): the daemon reads it, stores the blob (store.put_blob), runs crates/script, calls the core, appends figure_drawn and reply_landed. Errors keep the script's line:col and a hint; warnings print on success. --dry-run writes nothing and returns the frame, the parts, the warnings and the PNG.
Sizes: control/lib.rs 477, control/agent.rs 355, daemon/server.rs 474, daemon/tests.rs 476: new files control/src/figure.rs, daemon/src/server/figure.rs, cli/src/draw.rs, and tests in new files. A verb the app never sends is skip_serializing with its own type. Socket tests in crates/daemon/src/tests; CLI tests in crates/cli/src/tests. docs/service.md, docs/cli.md (table near :62), docs/app-parity.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and guide.md's command list in the same commit (tests/guide.rs fails on a missing command).

title: control, daemon, CLI: canvas redraw and canvas figure
description: slinger canvas redraw <CANVAS> <NAME> --data JSON|@FILE [--script FILE]: merge the data patch into the figure's last data (figure_drawn gives the script blob and data), run it again and replace in place; only what changed is written. slinger canvas figure <CANVAS> [NAME] [--script] [--data]: list figures, or print one's parts, script or data. Same four places and docs as canvas draw. Test: redraw with equal data writes no op; a redraw after the user wrote over a part leaves every stroke; a redraw by another agent is refused with the author rule's error.

title: agents know how: guide, both skills, the sling note and an e2e check
description: crates/cli/src/guide.md gains "draw a figure" as a common task with the script API reference (Appendix A of docs/design/figures.md) and one example; say when to draw and when plain text is right. Update plugin/skills/slinger/SKILL.md, plugin/skills/slinger-listen/SKILL.md (:37) and the sling note (snapshots in crates/core/tests/sling.rs change). tests/guide.rs parses every "slinger ..." line against clap: no flag that does not exist. scripts/e2e-sling.sh: add a sling that asks for a picture and check figure_drawn in the events with the check "$(jq ...)" pattern (:136, :172); run it by hand once (it spends tokens) and say so in the commit if it was not run. CHANGELOG under [Unreleased].

title: script API: small-model fluency round through canvas draw --dry-run
description: Repeat the spike's test on the real verb. Give a small model only the guide's API reference and five tasks with no example in it (e.g. a timeline from data, a kanban board, vector addition with a table and an answer area, a labelled state diagram, annotations over existing items with --over). Each script runs once through canvas draw --dry-run --png on a scratch daemon. A failure is fixed in the API or its error text, not in the script; a layout flaw becomes a warning or a better default. Record the tasks, results and changes in docs/design/figures.md "Fluency". Pass: five of five run first time and read correctly in the PNG. Spends tokens: note the model used.

title: tldraw import keeps fill and dash
description: crates/core/src/tldraw/map.rs (378 lines) drops a geo shape's fill and dash today. Map tldraw fill (none/semi/solid/pattern) and dash (draw/solid/dashed/dotted) to the new fields, and isLocked to locked. Test with a fixture; the reference worksheet (a locked scaffold of dashed and dotted boxes) is the real case. docs for the importer in the same commit.

title: acceptance: the worksheet from one script, redrawn by name, in the app
description: On a scratch daemon (own --socket, --data-dir, --scratch) with slinger-app --drive: canvas draw the Appendix B worksheet script; read the scene outline and the PNG. Draw strokes over two answer areas with slinger drive; canvas read shows over=figure/part for them. canvas redraw fills "actual top 5" by name. Check: every pen stroke is unchanged; the eraser and lasso pass over the scaffold; a second identical redraw writes no op; undo takes the figure away in one step. Fix what fails or file a seed for it. What only a person can judge (real pen feel over locked items, the look of fills and dashes, colours) goes in docs/hand-check.md.

title: owner review: hand checks and open picks, figures
description:

title: app: the nvim process made safe: own state and cache dirs, attach after ready, no lost text
description: Spike code: branch spike/nvim-embed (commit 892628c, pushed to origin, never to be merged); turn it on with SLINGER_NVIM=user or SLINGER_NVIM=clean. Do setup on VimEnter and attach the buffer only after a ready notification: before that, the user's config undid the setup and a buffer attach heard nothing, so every leave committed an empty text. A leave with no confirmed buffer keeps the old text. Tests: nothing written under the user's nvim dirs; an early leave, a crash and a failed start never lose the text. title: app: paint nvim's grid in the edited text's box: 80 cells, no gutter, no ruler
description: Spike code: branch spike/nvim-embed (commit 892628c, pushed to origin, never to be merged); turn it on with SLINGER_NVIM=user or SLINGER_NVIM=clean. The pure grid state and redraw reduction (crates/app/src/nvim/ in the spike), the painter in platform. 80 text cells: nonumber, norelativenumber, signcolumn=no set after the user's config (owner pick 2026-11-24), ruler and the last-row status hidden. A font fallback so nerd-font icons do not show as boxes (the spike used Menlo). The selection handles and the Sling/prompt/Delete bar are not drawn over a text being edited. The opaque box covering neighbours: say what shows through. The view after a paste past the cap stays scrolled until gg: fix. The scene outline (`slinger drive`) says the cells, mode and cursor.

title: app: keys while nvim edits a text: how it ends, app chords, paste, dictation, undo
description: Spike code: branch spike/nvim-embed (commit 892628c, pushed to origin, never to be merged); turn it on with SLINGER_NVIM=user or SLINGER_NVIM=clean. A new text starts in insert mode; ctrl+return in a text ends it and chains the next (as today). Escape in normal mode, :q and a press outside end the text and commit it (spike: all three pass). cmd chords stay with the app; cmd+z and cmd+shift+z map to nvim undo and redo while editing, and one app undo after the text ends undoes the whole edit. Paste and dictation through nvim_paste; clipboard=unnamedplus must reach the real clipboard (the spike's yanks went to a scratch file). Keys typed in the 75-107 ms before nvim is ready are queued, not dropped. Mouse press and drag reach nvim. The hint under the text and the key overlay name the ways out. Known cost: Esc-Esc from insert, and a normal-mode <Esc> mapping never fires.

title: core, app: a text is an 80-cell column that grows to 80 lines, then needs a step in
description: Per the design step. A text has a column 80 cells wide and grows down to 80 lines. Past the cap the item stops growing, shows a fade and 'N more lines', and a step in shows the rest (reuse the fold's step in and peek where it fits). The whole text is always in the packet. The core and the app must measure the same rows (slinger-ce52ee). An agent-written text follows the same cap.

title: app: a write-focus chord: fit the edited column to the pane, restore the view when the text ends
description: One command (registry, palette, overlay, menu): while a text is edited, zoom and pan the pane so the 80-cell column fits its width; ending the text restores the view. Hides the jump between the grid and the rendered view inside a view change.

title: app: a text not being edited draws as rendered markdown; a press edits at that word
description: Same string, second view. The subset from the design step: headings, emphasis, lists, quotes, code spans, checkboxes; no tables or images. Hard line breaks inside a paragraph join as markdown does. The width matches the 80-cell column. A press or double press on a word starts editing with the cursor on that word in the source. Pure layout in the scene; the fallback scene editor edits the source as today.

title: core, guide: an agent cannot change a text the user wrote; a reply lands beside it and stays short
description: The owner's column stays the owner's. The core refuses an agent's change to the characters of a text the user wrote (a stable error code and a hint naming where to put a reply); an agent may still place items beside it. crates/cli/src/guide.md and both skills say: reply beside the text, short, a question or a thing rather than prose. Check what a sling of a long text sends (text in the packet, picture or not). Owner pick 2026-11-24: absolute, no grant for one sling.
